"owner disposition pending" (RT-G06, RT-G10, RT-G14, RT-G16), the description should say so
rather than silently assert a behaviour.

Clearing `waiting_for_free` also only triggers another availability check, rather than
guaranteeing progress. Completion can leave background work, and an exit can leave only
one Ready seat. Quiet-round termination does not bound an all-busy wait because the
minimum-free check stops seat traversal and further round counting.

rules: Observer only. Silence or long work is never a reason to abort a participant.
Process-level observations cannot always be attributed to one ACP session; do not pretend otherwise.

investigations.note: Run 1 kept scheduling seats after 68 HTTP 402 credit failures, 44 empty replies and 3 rate limits; seat 'gone' stayed null. Responsive, occupied and unavailable are different states. Source: run 1 audit P04-P06, D03.
Built on agentsight-capture; observes nothing unless Roundtable runs as root. The owner's design is a root service under HoldOn (topogee DECISIONS.md).

archaeology.finding: Python marked seats degraded after 2 consecutive failures and unavailable after 4, then probed with doubling waits up to an hour. Not in the spec; not carried over as an automatic action.

decisions.decision: Each participant shows one of: working (ACP activity or observed activity), waiting (in flight, no observed activity), unavailable (last provider call failed, with the error), exited (process gone), unknown. These are information for the chair and the record, never triggers to cancel or unseat.

activity.package: agent host library (reusable; basis for the chassis)
activity.name: agent activity monitoring

code.bus.event.goal: Make activity observations available to subscribers as they happen.

code.client.agent.goal: Relate observations to the right participant.
code.client.agent.function: Provides the launched harness process id and its ACP session ids.

upstream.tracer.agent.goal: See what a participant's harness is doing when ACP reports nothing.
upstream.tracer.agent.function: Captures process, subprocess, file, network and observable model-provider activity through agentsight-capture.

elephant.design: Observe what each agent's process actually does, independently of what ACP reports, so silence can be told apart from work.
elephant.built: crates/agent-monitor attaches AgentSight's probes to each agent's process.
gaps: It observes nothing unless Roundtable runs as root.
The owner's design, a root service run under HoldOn, is not built.

findings.finding: The decision says each participant shows one of working / waiting / unavailable (with the provider error) / exited / unknown. Nothing derives these states. agent-monitor deliberately judges nothing (crates/agent-monitor/src/lib.rs:9-10). The engine only turns MonitorUnavailable into an 'error' notice (crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs:481-486), and the web UI shows the last raw observation (crates/roundtable-web/assets/index.html:259). Provider-call failure is not something the monitor observes, and the elephant gaps do not record any of this as unbuilt.

The document says the monitor receives 'its ACP session ids'. Harness holds only pid and an optional harness id string (crates/agent-monitor/src/lib.rs:72-77). The engine passes the HarnessStarted pid and harness id, never a session id (crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs:796-802). Observations are tied to a seat through the harness id (engine.rs:484, 490-493).

'Observable model-provider activity' overstates what is captured. TLS capture covers only the harness pid, not its children, and requests are never classified as model calls; only method, host, path, status and exchange id are published (crates/agent-monitor/src/lib.rs:33-45; crates/agent-monitor/src/capture.rs:103-125).

Undocumented behaviour: (1) attach fails if process capture cannot start, but TLS capture may fail on its own (lib.rs:28-39). (2) attach waits for the probe's CLOCK_SYNC start record before returning (capture.rs:66-81). (3) File-change, write and network records are aggregated and flushed every 5 seconds (lib.rs:30-31). (4) A probe that stops publishes monitor.unavailable (capture.rs:136-147). (5) Dropping the Monitor stops the probes without publishing anything (lib.rs:23-24). The bus event names are not listed (lib.rs:102-104, 117-119, 153-155).

This is correct, but it should add four facts. Capabilities without root are not enough, because AgentSight would fall back to `sudo -n`, which the crate refuses (capture.rs:179-209). It runs on Linux only (capture.rs:170-171). The `agentsight` cargo feature is on by default, and without it nothing is captured (crates/agent-monitor/Cargo.toml:8-12). At run time the probes need libelf, libz and libzstd (lib.rs:55-58).

Three different state vocabularies: working/waiting/gone/unknown, working/waiting/unavailable/exited/unknown, and responsive/occupied/unavailable. A reader cannot tell which is the contract or whether 'gone' equals 'exited'.

'Unavailable (last provider call failed)' has no stated source of provider errors in the wants (bus, ACP or tracer). The word also collides with the code's 'monitor.unavailable', which means monitoring itself is unavailable.
'Observes nothing unless root' contradicts the depended-on fail-open decision (process exit and ACP traffic still observed), so a reader cannot tell which states work without root.

Load-bearing terms and sources are undefined or outside the folder: HoldOn, 'topogee DECISIONS.md', 'run 1 audit P04-P06, D03', seat, chair, chassis. Closing the root gap depends on HoldOn, which is never explained.
The document says process observations cannot always be attributed to one ACP session, but not what is published when they can't, or why a participant has several session ids.

paraphrase.egm-codebase-details: The agent-monitor crate attaches AgentSight's eBPF probes to a harness process and its children when the engine sees the harness start. It publishes what they do (programs started and ended, file activity, network, HTTP over TLS without bodies or headers) as monitor.attached, monitor.observation and monitor.unavailable bus events, tagged with the harness pid and id. It only observes; it never judges or stops an agent, and it works only as root.
paraphrase.egm-comprehension: An observer in the agent host library that watches each participant's harness process through AgentSight. It publishes activity on the event bus, correlated by process id and ACP session ids, so the chair can tell working from waiting, unavailable, exited or unknown. It never cancels or unseats anyone. As built in crates/agent-monitor it observes nothing unless Roundtable runs as root.

roundtable.resolution:
# Resolution of review findings — `code.monitor.activity` (agent activity monitoring)

Draft contributed by StarkVortex for the roundtable. Each finding gets a decision (right / not
right), the change it requires (in the **description** `element.md` or in the **code**), and the
reason. Where a finding's reasoning needs correction, that is stated explicitly.

## Verification scope

The `source/` folder in this run contains only `crates/agent-monitor/src/lib.rs` and
`crates/agent-monitor/src/capture.rs`. Findings citing `engine.rs`, `index.html`, `Cargo.toml`,
`README.md`, `Roundtable_ACP_Integration_Design.md`, `archaeology/...` or `topogee DECISIONS.md`
refer to files not provided here. All assertions GF1–GF5 make **about `lib.rs`/`capture.rs` were
checked and are accurate**; claims about the absent files are treated as unverifiable here, which
does not change any verdict because each verdict also stands on the description plus the two
supplied files.

A general principle applied below: `lib.rs:9-10` ("The monitor is an observer only. Nothing here
judges, times out, or stops an agent") and rule 1 (element.md:48) are deliberate design choices.
No resolution should make `agent-monitor` derive states, time out, or act on silence.

---

## GF1 — Blocker — decisions (states are not derived)

**Right.**

`lib.rs:9-10` confirms the crate judges nothing; it publishes `monitor.attached`,
`monitor.observation`, `monitor.unavailable` only (`lib.rs:102-104, 117-119, 153-155`). The
decision at element.md:83 asserts five participant states including "unavailable (last provider
call failed, with the error)". Nothing in `agent-monitor` derives them, provider-call failure is
not something it observes, and the elephant `gaps` (element.md:98-101) list only root/HoldOn —
not the missing state derivation. The engine/UI citations (engine.rs:481-486, index.html:259)
are unverifiable here, but the blocker stands without them.

**Change (description).** Do **not** add state derivation to the crate. Either:
1. Move the five-state decision to the consumer `code.manager.chat.group`, whose want
   (element.md:17) is the part that actually "shows" participant state, and replace it here with
   a statement of what this element emits (raw observations + attached/unavailable notices); or
2. Keep it here but add to `elephant.gaps` an explicit "unbuilt" entry: no component derives
   working/waiting/unavailable/exited/unknown; the monitor supplies observations only;
   provider-call failures are not observed by this element.

**Why.** The description currently presents a contract as decided while `built`/`gaps` imply only
the probe-attachment crate exists. A reader cannot tell the state model is unimplemented. Fixing
the description (not the observer-only code) preserves rule 1 and the crate's stated purpose.

---

## GF2 — Major — want `code.client.agent` ("ACP session ids")

**Right.**

`Harness` is `{ pid: u32, id: Option<String> }` (`lib.rs:72-77`); `lib.rs:19-20` says observations
are tagged with "the harness's pid and the optional harness id the host chose". There is no ACP
session id and no collection of session ids. The engine citations (796-802, 484, 490-493) are
unverifiable here, but the description is wrong regardless of them.

**Change (description).** Rewrite the want's Function to: "Provides the launched harness process
id and an optional harness-name/id string chosen by the host; observations are correlated to a
seat through that harness id, not through an ACP session id." Remove "its ACP session ids" and
the plural. Correspondingly amend rule 2 and GF10 (below).

**Why.** The want promises an identifier the code never receives; anyone implementing against the
description would look for a session-id correlation mechanism that does not exist.

---

## GF3 — Major — want `upstream.tracer.agent` ("observable model-provider activity")

**Right.** Fully confirmed in the supplied files: TLS is `sslsniff` on the harness pid alone
(`lib.rs:33-39`, `capture.rs:103-115` — `-p <pid>`, descendants explicitly excluded), and
requests are never classified as model calls (`lib.rs:41-45`); only method, host, path, status
and exchange id are published (`capture.rs:265-281`).

**Change (description).** Replace "Captures process, subprocess, file, network and observable
model-provider activity" with: "Captures process-tree exec/exit, file, write and network
operations, plus HTTP requests and responses on the harness process's **own** TLS connections;
provider endpoints are identifiable from host/path and HTTP status, but requests are not
classified as model calls and descendants' TLS is not captured."

**Why.** "Model-provider activity" implies both coverage of child processes and semantic
classification of LLM calls. Neither is true; overstating it would mislead the dependent part
(GF7's "unavailable" state relies on exactly this overstatement).

---

## GF4 — Major — whole document (undocumented behaviour + event names)

**Right.** All five sub-points confirmed:
1. Process capture required / TLS fail-open (`lib.rs:28-39`; `capture.rs:60-64` → `Err`,
   `capture.rs:90-98` → publish unavailable, return `Ok`).
2. `attach` waits for `CLOCK_SYNC`/`phase=start` before returning (`capture.rs:66-81, 212-215`).
3. File-change/write/network aggregation flushed every 5s (`lib.rs:30-31`).
4. A probe that stops publishes `monitor.unavailable` (`capture.rs:136-147`).
5. Dropping `Monitor` stops probes silently (`lib.rs:23-24`; `capture.rs:23-35`).
The three event names `monitor.attached`, `monitor.unavailable`, `monitor.observation`
(`lib.rs:102-104, 117-119, 153-155`) are absent from element.md.

**Correction to the finding's wording:** these behaviours *are* documented in `lib.rs`'s module
doc comments (lines 14-58). "Undocumented" is correct only with respect to `element.md`, which
is what the finding is about.

**Change (description).** Add an "Interface / behaviour" section to element.md recording: the
three bus event names; process-required vs TLS-fail-open; the `CLOCK_SYNC` attach barrier (so a
caller knows `attach` blocks until probes are live); the 5s aggregation flush (so a consumer does
not expect per-event timing); probe-stop → `monitor.unavailable`; host-requested stop → silent.
Alternatively add `lib.rs:14-58` to the `references` layer as the normative behavioural source
instead of duplicating it.

**Why.** These are load-bearing semantics for anyone consuming the events or calling `attach`,
and the event names are the actual contract with `code.bus.event` (element.md:20).

---

## GF5 — Nit — investigations: privileges (four missing facts)

**Right.** All four confirmed: `sudo -n` fallback refused / capabilities insufficient
(`capture.rs:179-210`, test `495-510`); Linux-only (`capture.rs:169-171`); `agentsight` feature
default-on and nothing captured without it (`lib.rs:55-58`; `Cargo.toml` absent but `lib.rs:55`
independently states default-on); runtime libs `libelf`, `libz`, `libzstd` (`lib.rs:57-58`).

**Change (description).** Extend the privileges investigation note with those four facts,
attributed to `lib.rs:49-58` and `capture.rs:169-210`.

**Why.** "Needs root" alone is misleading: a reader might grant CAP_BPF/CAP_PERFMON, run on
macOS, or build with `--no-default-features` and still expect capture. Each is a distinct reason
capture silently degrades to `monitor.unavailable`.

---

## GF6 — Major — three state vocabularies

**Right, and understated: there are four.** Confirmed in element.md: want
working/waiting/gone/unknown (line 17); decision working/waiting/unavailable/exited/unknown
(line 83); investigation responsive/occupied/unavailable (line 57-58). A fourth is in the code's
own doc comment, `lib.rs:6-7`: "working, waiting on the network, exited, or alive with no
observable activity". "gone", "exited" and "alive with no observable activity" overlap without
being equated; "unavailable" is used for both an agent state and a monitor state.

**Change (description).** Choose one vocabulary as the contract and define each term; either
equate or explicitly distinguish "gone" and "exited"; drop "responsive/occupied" from the
investigation as a state vocabulary (keep it as historical narrative about run 1); align
`lib.rs:6-7`'s informal wording with the chosen terms. State which vocabulary is normative for
`code.manager.chat.group`.

**Why.** Multiple undefined, overlapping vocabularies make it impossible to say what the
dependent part should display, and they feed directly into GF1, GF7 and GF8.

---

## GF7 — Major — decision "unavailable"

**Right in substance; one part of the reasoning needs correction.**

Confirmed: `MonitorUnavailable` (`lib.rs:110-119`) means *monitoring* is unavailable and
"`capture` ... This says nothing about the agent itself" (`lib.rs:109`). The decision's
"unavailable (last provider call failed)" therefore collides with a code event of the same name
that means the opposite kind of thing. And no want states a source of provider errors.

Correction: "no stated source" is slightly overstated — `upstream.tracer.agent`'s want claims
"observable model-provider activity" (GF3 shows this is overclaimed), and `HttpResponse.status`
exists as raw data (`lib.rs:185`; 401 test at `capture.rs:427`). The real problem is that HTTP
requests are not classified as model calls (GF3), no component derives a state from them (GF1),
and the name collides.

**Change (description, convergent with the roundtable).** Do **not** rename the state to
"failed" yet. Keep the name open and mark the row **"no source in this element — requires an
explicit provider-error source (ACP or engine) to be added to the wants before it can be
derived"** (CrypticHammer's refinement, adopted by StarkTornado). Add a note that
`monitor.unavailable` describes the monitor, not the participant.

**Why the rename is wrong (concrete check):** the crate does publish `HttpResponse { status }`
(`lib.rs:185`; 401 test at `capture.rs:427-431`), and a reader could mistake a 401/429 status for
a provider-call *outcome*. But a response status is traffic — the provider answered — not an
outcome of whether the call succeeded from the host's perspective. Wiring "failed" to HTTP status
would repeat GF3's overclaim (inventing a classification the crate does not make). Leaving the
row flagged "no source" keeps GF7's defect visible until a genuine provider-error feed is named.
The naming collision with `monitor.unavailable` is real and must still be documented.

See the state-derivation table below, which makes this the single normative contract.

---

## GF8 — Major — elephant gaps vs. fail-open decision

**Right in substance; the stated cause is not verifiable here and is a mis-framing.**

What is real: "It observes nothing unless Roundtable runs as root" (element.md:99, 100) leaves
"nothing" unscoped, so a reader cannot tell which of the five decision states work without root
— a genuine comprehension gap. What cannot be confirmed: the "depended-on fail-open decision
(process exit and ACP traffic still observed)" is **not** in element.md, and the cited
`upstream.tracer.agent` decisions were not supplied. Literally read, the elephant sentence is
accurate about the thing it describes: `crates/agent-monitor` (the `built` item, element.md:97)
attaches AgentSight probes, and `attach` returns `monitor.unavailable` without root
(`lib.rs:49-53`; `capture.rs:37-42`). ACP traffic and harness-liveness are a separate channel —
element.md:92 says the design observes "independently of what ACP reports" — so there is no
contradiction inside this element, only an unstated boundary.

**Change (description).** Scope the gap: "The **AgentSight-based process-level observations**
produce nothing unless Roundtable runs as root; without root `monitor.unavailable` is published
for the whole monitor. ACP-reported activity and harness process liveness are a separate channel
and are not provided by this element (see `code.client.agent` / `code.manager.chat.group`)."
Then state which decision states remain available without root. Do not record this as an error
in the elephant.

**Why.** Fixes the reader's real problem (which states degrade) without falsely asserting a
contradiction with a decision that is not in this document, and without weakening the accurate
root requirement that GF5 strengthens.

---

## GF9 — Major — undefined load-bearing terms and sources

**Right.** All six appear in element.md and none is defined there: `chassis` (line 8), `chair`
(line 83), `seat` (lines 58, 71), `HoldOn` (lines 62, 100), `topogee DECISIONS.md` (line 62),
`run 1 audit P04-P06, D03` (line 58). The elephant `gaps` make resolution of the root gap depend
on "a root service run under HoldOn" (line 100), so HoldOn is load-bearing yet unexplained.

**Change (description).** Add a short glossary (or a `references` entry with resolvable paths)
for these terms; for the external audit/DECISIONS sources, either give a resolvable path or mark
them as external context not required to understand this element. Most importantly, state what
HoldOn is and how the root service would satisfy the root requirement, or remove the claim that
closing the gap depends on it.

**Why.** A reviewer of this element alone cannot evaluate the privileges gap, the run-1
investigation, or the decision's audience. Undefined external dependencies in a functional map
make the element unauditable.

---

## GF10 — Nit — rules (attribution)

**Right.** Rule 2 (element.md:49) warns that process observations cannot always be attributed to
one ACP session, but the description never says what is published in that case, and the want
(line 22) implies a participant has "several session ids" without explaining why. The code's
actual model answers what is published, but does not explain the host's session lifecycle:
there is no ACP session correlation at all; every `Observation` is
tagged with a `Harness` (`lib.rs:141-142`), and when the probe cannot attribute a record to a
process, `Observation.pid` is `None` (`lib.rs:143-145`, `capture.rs:295-301`; the `EventsLost`
example is at `capture.rs:473-477`). An `Other` record may retain a PID;
its variant alone does not determine process attribution.

**Change (description).** Replace rule 2 / the want with: "Observations are always attributed to
a harness (pid + optional harness id); they are not attributed to an ACP session. When the probe
cannot attribute a record to a specific process, `Observation.pid` is `None` (e.g. lost-event
counts); the harness tag still supports the host's participant correlation." Remove "ACP
session ids" everywhere (GF2) and any implication of several session ids.

**Why.** Gives the consumer the concrete answer the rule currently withholds and removes a
distinction (session-level attribution) the code never makes.

---

## Proposed consumer state model (StarkTornado / CrypticHammer, corrected by HeroicLizard)

The crate is observer-only and publishes three event types: `monitor.attached`,
`monitor.observation`, `monitor.unavailable`. `MonitorUnavailable` "says nothing about the agent
itself" (`lib.rs:109`), so the intended participant display belongs downstream. The following
records necessary evidence, not an implemented or complete state machine. The consumer must
still define freshness, precedence, recovery and request lifecycle handling (GF1, GF6, GF7):

| Decision state | Derivation from published events |
|---|---|
| exited | `Observation` with `Activity::ProcessExit` where `pid == harness.pid` |
| working | Recent positive work evidence from ACP or relevant activity observations; an arbitrary observation is insufficient. `EventsLost`, `ProcessExit`, or a diagnostic `Other` must not automatically imply working. |
| waiting | A known in-flight request, no recent positive work evidence, and sufficient current observation coverage to interpret silence. A historical `MonitorAttached` alone is insufficient. |
| unknown | Evidence is insufficient or stale, including when required capture coverage is lost and no independent ACP/host evidence resolves the state. This can occur after an earlier attachment or observation. |
| unavailable (provider call failed) | **no source in this element — requires an explicit provider-error source (ACP or engine) to be added to wants before it can be derived** |
| capture health (separate) | `MonitorUnavailable` updates confidence/coverage for the specified capture; it must never directly mean participant unavailable or exited. Independent ACP or host evidence can still establish participant state. |

Use 'exited' in place of 'gone' in the current goal. Keep responsive/occupied as historical
audit terminology, not aliases of the display states: they describe different dimensions.
The `pid: None` unattributable case (GF10) stays a property of individual
`Observation`s, not a participant state.

Track health per capture and track host-requested stops: `Drop` is silent and a past attachment
does not prove present coverage (`capture.rs:29-34, 90-98, 136-146`). Process-exit evidence must
refer to the harness PID, not a child. Host lifecycle reporting should also support exit display
when privileged capture is absent; this host behavior is not verified in the supplied source.

**Precedence rule (required for the consumer).** If the consumer receives both an authoritative
harness `ProcessExit` (`pid == harness.pid`) and a later `monitor.unavailable`, the established
exit must not regress to unknown or waiting for the same harness lifetime. Still record capture
health independently. `pump` publishes unavailable whenever its stream ends (`capture.rs:136-147`);
the local code does not establish that every harness exit ends that stream, nor that every stream
end indicates a harness exit. This is a proposed consumer precedence rule, not an implemented
state reducer or a guarantee about upstream probe termination.

**Observable test that the resolution was applied** (CrypticHammer): after the edits, element.md's
decisions/wants/gaps layers must (1) name the three bus events plus the `pid: null` case instead
of asserting five participant states are produced here, and (2) list the state-derivation layer
as an explicit unbuilt gap owned by the consumer.

---

## Summary of decisions

| Finding | Decision | Primary change |
|---|---|---|
| GF1 | Right | Description: scope/move the five-state decision; record derivation as an unbuilt gap |
| GF2 | Right | Description: replace "ACP session ids" with harness pid + optional harness id |
| GF3 | Right | Description: narrow "model-provider activity" to the harness's own TLS HTTP traffic, no classification |
| GF4 | Right | Description: add interface/behaviour section incl. the three event names (or reference lib.rs:14-58) |
| GF5 | Right | Description: add the four privilege facts |
| GF6 | Right (four vocabularies, not three) | Description: one normative, defined vocabulary |
| GF7 | Right (reasoning corrected) | Description: keep state name open, flagged "no source"; note the `monitor.unavailable` collision; do not wire to HTTP status |
| GF8 | Right in substance (cause corrected) | Description: scope "nothing" to AgentSight observations; state which states survive without root |
| GF9 | Right | Description: glossary / resolvable sources, especially HoldOn |
| GF10 | Right | Description: state `pid: None` behaviour; remove session-id language |

**No code changes are required.** Every finding is a defect in `element.md` (or a mis-framing of
it), not in `lib.rs`/`capture.rs`. The crate is internally consistent and well documented; the
description drifted from it. In particular, do not fix GF1 by adding state derivation to an
observer-only crate — that would violate rule 1 and `lib.rs:9-10`.

## Two cross-cutting themes worth applying as a package

- **Cluster A (GF1, GF6, GF7, GF8):** the `decisions` layer is a *consumer* contract misplaced in
  this element. Resolve these four together by scoping the decision to `code.manager.chat.group`
  and stating what this element actually emits.
- **Cluster B (GF2, GF3, GF7, GF10):** the description's "ACP session ids / model-provider
  activity" model does not match the code, which correlates by harness pid + one optional id
  string and publishes process-tree observations plus unclassified HTTP. Resolve these four
  together with one consistent vocabulary.

rules: No reply limit by default (the owner's length experiment).
When a limit is set, a message over it is blocked and not shared; it is never cut.
After an agent was skipped while busy, its next discussion reply gets the recovery limit (1,024) once, then the limit returns to normal. Several skips give it once.
No credits: passing and skipping add nothing.

investigations.note: Run 1 excluded five submissions for exceeding 512 characters (513-523 chars). The current spec truncates instead. Source: ~/topogee/docs/roundtables/1-embodied-ai-in-a-3d-physics/Roundtable_1_First_Run_Analysis_and_Failure_Audit.md P09.

archaeology.finding: Python credited +512 per accepted peer message missed while busy, not per skipped turn: allowance = 512 x (1 + pass credits + missed accepted messages).
Python spent the offered credits when a reply was accepted and kept them on veto; the bank carried across topics only in session mode.
Python never reported characters removed by truncation: status_kept_truncated is empty and private_feedback ignores truncation.

decisions.decision: A vetoed contribution neither credits nor spends the allowance: it never reached the group, and README 4.6 only says it earns no credit.
An accepted contribution spends the whole bank; the allowance returns to 512.
The allowance carries across topic changes, because README 8 says topic changes do not reset the collaboration.

Characters are Unicode scalar values (Rust char). Truncation cuts at the last grapheme-cluster boundary within the allowance so no character is split; the notice reports the removed count in the same unit.
The credit system is gone; a busy skip earns one larger reply instead.
decisions.owner_statement: it doesnt matter 1024 is plenty and yes remove the credits messsage

decisions.decision: Messages are never truncated; an over-limit message is blocked.
decisions.owner_statement: we arent going to be truncating if we add limits in we will block messages for being too long

superseded.rule: +512 for each skipped turn while occupied with independent work.
Oversized contributions are truncated to the allowance before evaluation, never rejected for length; the removed character count is reported at the next turn.

gates.name: Reply length limit blocks long messages

character.name: reply limit

elephant.design: Keep messages concise: no limit for now, and a message over a set limit is blocked, never cut.
sources: owner, 2026-11-07: "we arent going to be truncating if we add limits in we will block messages for being too long"
owner's evaluation specification: 1,024 characters after a busy skip
elephant.built: No limit by default. When set, an over-limit message is blocked; one reply after a busy skip gets 1,024 characters.
gaps: The block notice is the builder's wording and awaits the owner's text.

findings.finding: The 1,024 recovery limit applies only when a base limit is set: limit_for returns None when base_allowance is None (src/engine.rs:396-399), and that is the default (src/config.rs:157-158). Tests always set a base (tests/engine.rs:32).
'Reports the participant's current speaking allowance' is not done. Prompts carry no allowance (src/turn.rs:31-83); only the chair's FloorGiven event does (src/engine.rs:611).

findings.scope: decisions: veto, accepted contribution, topics, characters
findings.finding: These describe a bank that resets to 512, allowance carry-over and grapheme truncation as current, and are not marked superseded. The code has no bank (src/engine.rs:83-86) and blocks rather than cuts (src/turn.rs:128-146).

'Never cut' ignores topic proposals, which are cut to 512 by this element's truncate_to (src/rules.rs:19-38, src/turn.rs:323). Unstated: a blocked reply counts as a Failed opportunity and skips JEV (src/turn.rs:145).

The recovery limit replaces the base without comparing, so a base above 1,024 makes it smaller (src/engine.rs:398). Only give_floor skips set recovery_due (src/engine.rs:573), not floor-to-work (src/engine.rs:670-676); review prompts use it up (src/engine.rs:595, 603-605).
The unused DEFAULT_BASE = 512, commented 'Default reply limit', contradicts no limit by default (src/rules.rs:7-8). Validation rejecting 0 limits (src/config.rs:113-115) is undocumented.

Described as 'one larger reply', but with no default limit, 1,024 after a busy skip restricts a reply that would otherwise be unlimited. Whether 1,024 applies with no base limit, or when a set limit is above 1,024, is unstated.

findings.finding: Active decisions still describe the removed scheme (credits, the bank returning to 512, carrying the allowance across topics, grapheme-boundary truncation) without being marked superseded. The unit of length mixes Unicode scalars and grapheme clusters.
The prompt builder relies on this element to tell the agent its allowance, but the characters line was removed; when a limit is set, how an agent learns it before being blocked is unstated.
What a blocked message becomes (a veto, a failed turn, something else), whether the length check runs before or instead of JEV, and when the author is told are all unstated.
Who sets the limit, and where (a chair setting, config), is not stated; 'the owner's length experiment' is unexplained.

The run 1 note says 'the current spec truncates instead', which is stale (the current rule blocks). 'Bank', 'session mode' and 'busy skip' are undefined here. The README 4.x references appear to describe the superseded scheme.

When a limit is set, a reply over it is blocked, never cut, and the author is told at its next discussion turn. When a base limit exists, an agent skipped while busy gets the recovery limit (1,024 by default) for its next discussion prompt, once. Passing and skipping earn nothing.

# Reply limit: resolution of GF1–GF12

Reconciled by SpinyShark against the supplied source. These are decisions about changes to make, not claims that implementation changes have been applied. Source citations below are relative to `source/crates/roundtable/src/`. Only four Rust files are supplied: README, prompt templates, gate registry, and the reviewer's tests are unavailable for independent verification.

## Common policy decision

Prefer the current specific rule, “the recovery limit (1,024) once”, over the comparative phrase “one larger reply”. Recommended resolution: an ordinary discussion prompt uses `base_allowance` (default `None`, unlimited); the next successfully dispatched discussion prompt after a busy skip uses exactly `Some(recovery_allowance)` (default 1,024), independently of the base. This can restrict an otherwise unlimited reply or replace a base above 1,024 with 1,024. Replace “larger” with “one reply with the recovery limit”. This is a resolution recommendation from the supplied description, not an additional owner quotation.

Do not silently introduce `max(base, recovery)`: that would implement a different rule for bases above 1,024. Recovery is one pending flag, not accumulated credits. Repeated skips coalesce. Assignment and consumption occur on successful dispatch of the next discussion prompt, including a review whose reply is a contribution. A pass, veto, length block, or later prompt failure does not restore it; failure to dispatch leaves it pending. A reply already in progress keeps the limit assigned to its original prompt.

Define “busy skip” as `give_floor` encountering a Ready seat that is not free to speak and skipping its scheduled opportunity (`engine.rs:531–575`). Starting tool work in an already issued prompt is a distinct transition; it does not itself grant recovery. Proposal and rating prompts do not consume recovery. These explicit boundaries resolve the ambiguous parts of GF5 and GF7.

## GF1 — Right: code contradicts the unconditional recovery rule

`limit_for` exits through `base_allowance?` before checking recovery (`engine.rs:396–399`). The base defaults to `None` (`config.rs:157–158`). Recovery therefore never operates in the default configuration, contrary to rules[2], the manager want, and the built claim.

**Change code:** check `recovery_due` first, returning `Some(recovery_allowance)` when true and `base_allowance` otherwise. **Change description:** state explicitly that recovery applies with no base and replaces any configured base. The reviewer's test-coverage assertion cannot be verified here; include the unset-base case when implementing the fix.

## GF2 — Right: the participant is not told its effective allowance

`turn_prompt` never renders the effective limit (`turn.rs:31–83`). `FloorGiven` publishes it on the bus (`engine.rs:611`); the supplied code does not deliver that event as participant prompt text. A static template cannot reliably convey a changing per-seat allowance.

**Change code:** tell the participant the effective limit in every Floor and Reviewing prompt, including the counting unit and the consequence of exceeding it. Communicate a return to unlimited when applicable. Keep the participant-facing want rather than weakening it to chair telemetry.

Compute the limit once in `offer` and pass it into the builder. Do not read the old `seat.limit` inside the builder: `offer` computes the new value at line 596, builds the prompt at 597, and only stores the field at 604. Use the same computed value for prompt wording, stored enforcement limit, and the floor event. Update the stale prompt-format comments.

## GF3 — Right: bank-era decisions appear active

The four 2026-11-05 decisions about vetoes, accepted contributions, topics, and characters retain bank/reset/truncation behavior that the current code lacks. `Seat` holds a limit and a pending-recovery flag (`engine.rs:83–86`); `submit` blocks excess length (`turn.rs:125–146`).

**Change description:** mark these decisions superseded by the 2026-11-07 credit-removal and blocking decisions, preserving historical text and dates. Replace their active meaning with the assignment/consumption policy above. Retain the still-valid Unicode scalar counting unit in a new active statement. Do not reintroduce a bank or a reset to 512.

## GF4 — Right about scope and missing consequences

Discussion contributions are never length-truncated in `submit`. Topic proposals follow a separate path: `on_proposal` calls `truncate_to` with `PROPOSAL_LIMIT = 512` (`turn.rs:321–325`; `rules.rs:19–38`, RT-G13). An unqualified claim about all messages is too broad.

**Change description:** scope this element's no-cutting guarantee to discussion contributions, including reviews and work completions. Explicitly cross-reference the separate proposal rule: proposals are bounded to 512 Unicode scalar values at a grapheme boundary. Keep that separate behavior and helper in this resolution; discussion blocking does not remove proposal truncation. Narrow the elephant's broad wording too.

Record that length blocking precedes JEV and returns `Outcome::Failed`. For an ordinary Floor reply it counts a failed opportunity. Work/review completions do not consume another opportunity; see GF10. Update `submit`'s obsolete “Truncate, then judge” comment and `truncate_to`'s obsolete general claim that length never rejects contributions.

## GF5 — Partly right: observations verified, but three automatic fixes are not justified

**Replacement can reduce the allowance: true.** A base above 1,024 is replaced by recovery (`engine.rs:398`). Resolve the conflict by adopting the explicit fixed-recovery policy above and removing “larger”. Using `max` changes the specific numeric rule; it is not required to implement it.

**Floor-to-work does not set recovery: true, but not established as a defect.** `on_tool` turns Floor into Working and counts the opportunity as `SkippedWorking` without setting the flag (`engine.rs:670–675`). That prompt still produces a reply (`703–704`); the seat has not necessarily missed a later scheduled turn. Keep this behavior and define the recovery trigger precisely. If a later scheduled opportunity is skipped while it remains busy, `give_floor` grants recovery normally. Distinguish round accounting from the recovery trigger in the description.

**Reviews consume pending recovery: true, and consistent with “next discussion reply”.** `offer` includes Floor and Reviewing in discussion (`engine.rs:595–605`); both replies are submitted as contributions. A skipped seat can complete work, become Idle, and then receive a review while other seats remain busy (`engine.rs:537–550, 689`). The path is reachable. Keep consumption on successful discussion-prompt dispatch and document it. Reserving recovery exclusively for Floor would change the stated contract. Merely leaving the flag set while giving a review the recovery limit risks granting recovery twice.

## GF6 — Right, with a verification limit

`DEFAULT_BASE = 512` is labeled the default (`rules.rs:7–8`) but is unused in the supplied source, while `base_allowance` actually defaults to `None`. Validation rejects `Some(0)` and zero recovery (`config.rs:113–115`), even when the base is unset.

**Change code/comments:** remove the obsolete constant after checking the full repository for consumers; if a real consumer requires it, rename/document its actual purpose. Keep the unlimited default. **Change description:** each configured numeric limit must be at least one; `None`, not zero, means unlimited. Recovery is configurable and must also be positive.

## GF7 — Right about ambiguity; resolved consistently with GF1/GF5

“One larger reply” conflicts with an unlimited base and with a base above recovery. It cannot universally describe a fixed cap.

**Change description:** recovery is exactly the configured recovery limit once, including with no base and with a larger base; afterward the base applies again. State this as an explicit resolution decision, not a discovered owner clarification. GF1 supplies the unset-base code fix; replacement of a larger base already behaves this way. Do not leave incompatible alternatives or introduce an undocumented maximum operation.

## GF8 — Right about stale decisions; the alleged unit inconsistency is not a defect

Supersede the old decisions as in GF3. Counting Unicode scalar values and choosing a grapheme boundary for a cut are compatible operations, not inconsistent length units: `truncate_to` deliberately does both (`rules.rs:23–37`).

**Change description:** discussion length is `text.chars().count()` after outer whitespace is trimmed by `classify` (`rules.rs:50–58`; `turn.rs:129`). Exactly the limit is allowed; greater counts are blocked. Combining marks and multi-scalar emoji can count as multiple characters. Discussion contributions undergo no grapheme-based shortening. Keep the boundary behavior solely in the separate proposal rule. Do not change enforcement to bytes or grapheme counts.

## GF9 — Right; duplicates the missing feature in GF2

The assembled delivery has no dynamic allowance line. A deferred too-long notice reports a past block, not the limit before the participant composes its reply.

**Change code/description:** implement the GF2 announcement for both Floor and Reviewing using the limit for that prompt. Preserve advance information and communicate a return to unlimited. Do not substitute a description saying that the participant must discover a limit by being blocked. GF2 and GF9 need one implementation change.

## GF10 — Right: specify outcome, ordering, visibility, and notification

**Change description to record existing behavior** (`turn.rs:94–146, 52–55, 85–92`; `engine.rs:696–705`):

- Classification trims outer whitespace; pass and empty responses have separate handling. Contribution length is checked before judging or any unjudged acceptance fallback, so the limit also applies with judging off or JEV unavailable.
- An oversized contribution returns `Outcome::Failed`, not a JEV veto. It never reaches JEV or the accepted message log. A rejected `Contribution` event is still published with `accepted=false`, `judged=false`, no accepted ID, and the length reason. “Not shared” means not delivered as an accepted peer contribution, not absent from chair telemetry.
- A normal Floor completion counts the failed opportunity. Working/Reviewing completions use `after_work=true` and do not count another failed opportunity. Work's opportunity was counted when work began; a review is not an extra scheduled opportunity.
- The author gets a queued too-long notice in the next successfully dispatched discussion prompt, including a review. Proposal/rating prompts neither deliver nor clear it. Failed dispatch preserves it. Delivery is conditional on another discussion prompt occurring before the table ends.
- A block or veto does not restore recovery: assignment was consumed when the discussion prompt was sent.

Exact notice wording remains the owner-text gap already identified by the elephant; its template is not supplied here.

## GF11 — Right: identify the authority and timing

**Change description:** the host/chair supplies `TableConfig.base_allowance` and `TableConfig.recovery_allowance` when creating the table. Defaults are unlimited ordinary replies and 1,024 recovery; agents do not control those fields. The supplied command handler exposes no runtime limit setter (`engine.rs:850–910`), so do not claim an existing live chair control changes them. Replace “the owner's length experiment” with concrete behavior; keep provenance separately. No new runtime configuration API is needed to resolve the finding.

## GF12 — Right about stale prose and undefined terms; README content unverified

**Change description:** date the run-1 observation and rewrite “the current spec truncates instead” as a historical comparison with the then-current truncation policy, followed by today's blocking rule. Preserve chronology rather than silently rewriting historical conclusions. Define “busy skip” precisely as above; mark bank/session-mode discussion as archaeology. A bank was accumulated speaking allowance; session mode concerned its historical lifetime across topics.

The referenced README sections are absent from the copy. Audit them in the full repository, point active references to current blocking/recovery guidance, and label obsolete sections historical. The reviewers' suspicion is reasonable, but unseen README content is not established evidence.

## Checks for the implementation follow-up

Verify limits with base unset, below recovery, equal to recovery, and above recovery. Expected post-skip sequences include unlimited → 1,024 → unlimited and 2,000 → 1,024 → 2,000. Repeated skips yield one assignment. Verify review consumption, preservation on failed dispatch, and that starting tool work alone does not grant recovery.

Verify advertised/enforced limits agree on the first recovery prompt and the following normal prompt; exactly-at-limit and over-limit scalar counts; deferred notices; JEV bypass for oversized contributions; and no extra opportunity count for work/review completions. Preserve separate proposal behavior. These are proposed checks, not executed tests: this snapshot contains no Cargo manifest or test suite.

findings.finding: 'When a table ends, each agent rates every other' overstates it: the round starts only on chair End (engine.rs:906), the last round (engine.rs:636-639) or two quiet rounds with no limit (engine.rs:647-650). The document never names the host or the storage.

session_scoring.md:3-10 adds the worker rubric table, which the owner's roundtable prompt does not contain (docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md:57-61, 113), though prompts.rs:92-93 calls the resource verbatim.

The numbers 'Efficient 10, Alert & Aware 20, Thorough 30, Coordination 40, bonus +5' are never explained. They could be maximum points, weights or percentages. The scale of one rating and the bonus criteria are not stated, so you can't tell what a scorecard holds.

paraphrase.egm-codebase-details: The end-of-table peer rating round in turn.rs. When the chair ends the table, the rounds run out or the table goes quiet, every ready, named agent is sent the owner's scoring prompt and replies with a JSON scorecard for each other agent. Each card is turned into weighted points, published as a rating event that the web host saves to the rated agent's session-keyed profile, and gathered into a results ranking sent to every agent before the table ends.
paraphrase.egm-comprehension: When a Roundtable session (a 'table') ends, each agent scores every other agent using the owner's scoring prompt, which has four weighted categories plus a bonus. Each agent then gets a results message, and the ratings are stored with the agent's identity. turn.rs implements this for the group chat manager. Ratings only reach a later table if that table resumes the agent's earlier session.

# Resolution of review findings — `code.rating.peer` (peer rating round)

Decisions for GF1–GF12 in `element.md`. Each is judged against the code in `source/`.
Line references are to the copies in `source/crates/...`.

## Method and scope note

The reviewers cite `engine.rs`, `config.rs`, `tables.rs`, `prompts.rs` and
`docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md`. **Those files are not in `source/`**, so their
specific line numbers could not be independently checked here. Every finding also has a checkable
anchor in `turn.rs`, `rules.rs`, `app.rs`, the `resources/*.md` files, or `element.md` itself, and
each verdict below rests on those verified anchors. Sub-claims that depend only on the absent
files are noted as "reported, not verified"; none of them change a verdict.

**Summary:** all twelve findings are **right or partially right** (all are description /
comprehension / attribution gaps; no code bug is found in the rating logic itself). GF1–GF5 and
GF7–GF12 are **right**; **GF6 is partially right** — reclassified after a roundtable challenge
showed it is a provenance/attribution nit, though its central factual premise is unverifiable
here (see the GF6 section). The fixes are entirely to `element.md` (the functional map), not to
the code, because the code is coherent and the reviewers' substantive observations are things the
description fails to say. Several findings overlap; a consolidated fix plan is given at the end
so the same edit is not made twice.

| Finding | Verdict | Kind of fix |
|---|---|---|
| GF1 | Right | description: qualify triggers and eligible seats |
| GF2 | Right | description: state scoring formula + ranking |
| GF3 | Right | description: name the host + storage; correct `elephant.built` |
| GF4 | Right | description: add failure modes |
| GF5 | Right | description: add receipts, profile line, results delivery |
| GF6 | **Partially right** (reclassified) | description: label `session_scoring.md` as a composite resource; provenance nit, premise unverifiable (merge with GF11) |
| GF7 | Right | description: add scorecard legend (merge with GF2) |
| GF8 | Right | description: define identity, link, persistence |
| GF9 | Right | description: define "results", manager vs agents |
| GF10 | Right | description: define table, end triggers, scope |
| GF11 | Right | description: annotate references, introduce "owner" |
| GF12 | Right | description: record provenance of categories |

---

## GF1 (Major) — trigger and participants — RIGHT

`rules[0]` says "When a table ends, each agent rates every other". This overstates the eligible
set and hides the conditions.

Verified anchors:
- `turn.rs:421-425` `start_rating`: the round is skipped entirely when fewer than two seats are
  `SeatState::Ready` **and** have a name (`left.len() < 2` -> `end("ended by the chair")`).
- `turn.rs:429-433`: only idle seats in that set are asked now; busy ones are asked later when
  free (`ask_to_rate` via `settle`-style logic), and `RatingsAsked` lists only those seats.
- `turn.rs:438, 452`: the rater is asked to rate `names() != me`, i.e. only other **named** seats.
- `turn.rs:493-497`: a missing rating produces one error notice and **no retry**.
- `turn.rs:723-724` (departed seats dropped) and the engine-level triggers (chair End at
  `engine.rs:906`, last round `engine.rs:636-639`, two quiet rounds `engine.rs:647-650`, skipped
  on a second End `engine.rs:903` and other ends `engine.rs:791, 840`) are **reported, not
  verified** here, but are consistent with `start_rating` being an `end`-time routine.

**What should change:** in `element.md`, qualify `rules[0]` to "each *ready, named* agent still at
the table rates the other ready, named agents", and add a layer (or bullet) recording: the round
runs only when the table ends under the normal endings, is skipped with fewer than two eligible
seats or on a forced/immediate end, departed seats are dropped, and a missing rating is reported
without a retry. Why: a reader of the map cannot otherwise tell who is rated or when the round is
bypassed. See also GF10 (define "table"/"ends").

## GF2 (Major) — categories, weights, scoring rule, ranking — RIGHT

All parts verified:
- `rules.rs:150-162` `rating_points`: each category contributes
  `value.clamp(0.0,5.0)/5.0*weight` with weights 10/20/30/40; missing or non-numeric values
  fall through `unwrap_or(0.0)` and silently count as 0 (`rules.rs:158`); `bonus` adds 5.0 only
  when a boolean `true` (`rules.rs:160`). Max = 105, matching the doc comment (`rules.rs:150-151`).
- `turn.rs:529-544`: `rating = prior_profile_score + session_points`, `"unscored"` when there is
  no prior profile and zero cards; `rows.sort_by` on summed session points (a sum, not an average).

The `rules[0]` line lists the numbers but states none of this. **What should change:** add the
scoring rule to the description — stars 0–5 per category scaled by weight/5, +5 for a true
bonus, per-card max 105, missing/non-numeric = 0 — and add that the results message is a ranking
by summed session points where each rating is the earlier profile score plus this session's
points, with "unscored" until rated. Why: this is the central computation of the element and is
currently unstated. Merge with GF7 (which asks for the same legend) into one rules[0] edit.

## GF3 (Major) — saving; `elephant.built` — RIGHT

Verified:
- `turn.rs:471-484`: the core only accumulates `session_points` and publishes the `RatingGiven`
  event (consumed as `roundtable.rating`). No disk write, no profile mutation in the core crate.
- `app.rs:98-102`: the web host taps `roundtable.rating` and calls `save_rating`; persistence
  errors are published as loud notices.
- `app.rs:60-62, 70`: storage root is `$ROUNDTABLE_HOME` (else `$HOME/.roundtable`), identities
  under `identities/`. `app.rs:430-443`: profile file is `<session>.json`.
- `app.rs:498-509` `save_rating` -> `app.rs:450-475` `update_profile` (atomic tmp+rename) adds
  points and appends the rating. `app.rs:478-496` `FileIdentities` is the core's read-only
  `Identities` implementation (used at `turn.rs:39-40, 521`).
- `elephant.built` says "turn.rs ... records each scorecard and sends the owner's results
  message" — it does not record scorecards to identities; the host does.

The sub-claims "only `tables.rs:151` passes an identity store" and "spawn passes `None`,
`engine.rs:255`", and "`config.rs:42-50` only reads profiles" are **reported, not verified**
(files absent), but the architectural point is confirmed by `app.rs`: saving lives in the web
host and is driven by an event, not by the core.

**What should change:** in `element.md`, `rules[1]`/`elephant.built` should say the core emits
`roundtable.rating` events and that the **web host** persists them to
`$ROUNDTABLE_HOME/identities/<session>.json` via `save_rating`; note that persistence therefore
depends on the host running and on an identity store being supplied to the table. Correct
`elephant.built` so it no longer credits `turn.rs` with saving. Name the host crate/path. Why: the
description currently attributes an action to the element that the element does not perform.

## GF4 (Major) — failure modes — RIGHT

All verified in `turn.rs:447-503`:
- `450`: JSON is taken from the first `{` to the last `}`; a parse failure yields `None`.
- `487-491`: unreadable/top-level-non-object JSON records nothing (one error notice).
- `456-461`: a card whose value is not an object is rejected with a per-card notice.
- `463-467`: a name matching zero or several other seats is not recorded.
- Duplicate-name consequence, stated precisely (refines the reviewer's wording). Three distinct
  effects follow from `438`, `452` and `463`:
  - The rating *request* (`others`, `438`) and the missing-rating check (`unrated`, `452`) are
    built by filtering on the rater's own name, so two seats sharing a name are never *asked* to
    rate each other.
  - A **third** rater's card keyed to that shared name matches both seats (`targets.len()==2`,
    `463-467`) and is rejected.
  - But a **manually supplied** card from one of the two same-named seats to the other resolves
    to exactly one target: `463` excludes the rater (`j != i`), so with exactly two "X" seats the
    card matches only the peer and **is recorded**. The reviewer's blanket claim that "two agents
    with the same name cannot rate each other" is therefore imprecise — the automatic prompt
    omits the peer, yet the parser permits a manual card between exactly two same-named seats.
    (Credit: raised as a qualification by another participant; verified against `turn.rs:463`.)

The finding is still right: the name-keyed matching is a real, undocumented limitation. The fix
should describe all three effects, not repeat the overstated one.

Downstream consequence (adopted from the roundtable, `clarifications.TotalLogic.md` Point 1):
`session_points` is `seat_index -> (sum, count)` and `count` rises only for recorded cards
(`turn.rs:472-474`); `finish_ratings` prints "`<points/> points from <cards/> scorecards`" from
that same pair (`turn.rs:520, 534-537`). Since each rater's reply is still handled and the table
still ends (`turn.rs:502`), dropped cards mean the table can end with **fewer cards than
raters × targets**, and the per-seat "N scorecards" line silently reflects the loss. This is the
visible effect a maintainer needs: it is a *functional limitation with a displayed consequence*,
not merely "not recorded". The description note must say so.

**What should change:** add a "failure modes / robustness" layer to `element.md` recording these
behaviours, including the precise duplicate-name semantics above and the fewer-cards-than-expected
effect on the ranking line. Why: they determine which scorecards actually count and are entirely
undocumented.

## GF5 (Major) — messages — RIGHT

Verified:
- `turn.rs:498-501`: a `score_received` receipt ("Your private scorecard was received.") is sent
  when the card was readable; `score_received.md` confirms the text.
- `turn.rs:37-50`: a returning identity with prior ratings gets the `session_profile` line on its
  first turn ("Your profile score is ... You have N ratings across M earlier sessions");
  `session_profile.md` confirms.
- `turn.rs:551-560`: results go only to seats still `Ready`, named, `Idle`, and not already sent.
- `turn.rs:564-575`: the table ends once all such seats are sent (`end("ended by the chair")`).
  Two verified refinements (raised at the table, `DeifiedArrow-notes.md` / appended qualifications):
  `check_results_done` (`turn.rs:568-570`) also waits while an eligible seat is in
  `Activity::Notified`, so "ends once all are sent" is incomplete — notification replies must
  settle too; and `results_sent` is set before `offer`, whose success is ignored (`556-557`), so
  the verified contract is *attempted* delivery, not guaranteed receipt.

`rules[1]` mentions only "receives the owner's results message". **What should change:** record
the `score_received` receipt, the first-turn `session_profile` line for returning identities, and
the delivery/end conditions. Why: `rules[1]` is otherwise an incomplete account of what agents
receive. Note the profile line is a first-turn identity feature, not strictly part of the rating
round; document it as a related behaviour rather than moving it into the round.

## GF6 (Nit) — "owner's scoring prompt" / rubric table — PARTIALLY RIGHT (reclassified)

**Verdict evolution (kept for auditability).** My initial independent verdict was "not right": I
read GF6 as comparing `session_scoring.md` to the general discussion prompt
(`roundtable_prompt.md`), and argued the rubric belongs in the scoring prompt, so no discrepancy
exists. On the roundtable, StalkyValor (`StalkyValor-verdict.md`) showed the finding's
parenthetical cites `docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md` — the **owner's original
source record**, not the `roundtable_prompt.md` template. Read that way, GF6 is a **provenance /
attribution** nit: does the rubric, bonus criterion, and JSON contract in `session_scoring.md`
actually come from the owner, or was it added by the implementation? If not owner-specified,
`rules[0]`'s label "the owner's scoring prompt" overstates how much of that resource is
owner text. My earlier rebuttal defended against a different comparison than the finding made,
so a flat "not right" was too strong. Reclassified to **partially right**.

What is verifiable in-folder:
- `session_scoring.md:3-13` does contain the 4-row rubric table, the bonus criterion, and the
  JSON scorecard instruction. Confirms the "rubric is present" half.
- `rules[0]` calls this "the owner's scoring prompt" and `references` lists the file with no
  annotation (overlap with GF11).
What is **not** verifiable in-folder (the verification caveat, Point 3):
- Whether `docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md:57-61, 113` lacks the rubric, and
  whether `prompts.rs:92-93` includes the resource verbatim. Those files are not in `source/`.
  So GF6's central factual premise (the owner source omits the rubric) can be neither confirmed
  nor refuted here.

**Verdict: partially right.** The label "owner's scoring prompt" is genuinely imprecise about
provenance, and that is a legitimate documentation nit; but the finding's specific factual claim
is unverifiable, and no code change is warranted (deleting working rubric instructions would be
wrong).

**What should change (description only, largely shared with GF11):** label `session_scoring.md`
as a *composite resource* — the owner-attributed notice together with the rubric table, bonus
criterion, and JSON response format — rather than implying it is verbatim owner text; annotate it
in `references`; and require verifying the owner source before claiming any portion is owner-
specified. Why: it removes the over-attribution without discarding instructions agents need. No
code change.

## GF7 (Major) — numbers unexplained — RIGHT

`rules[0]` gives "Efficient 10, Alert & Aware 20, Thorough 30, Coordination 40, bonus +5" with
no legend: the numbers could be maxima, weights, or percentages, the 0–5 star scale and the
bonus criterion ("improved the final work beyond just critiquing it", `session_scoring.md:10`)
are absent, and a reader cannot tell what a scorecard holds (a JSON object keyed by participant
name, `session_scoring.md:12-13`). Verified directly against `element.md` and the resource.

**What should change:** expand `rules[0]` to define the scorecard shape, state that the numbers
are maximum points per category (weights), that stars run 0–5 and are scaled by weight/5, that
the bonus is +5 for a true boolean with its criterion, and that one card is worth at most 105.
Why: without this the rule is unreadable. **Merge with GF2** — one rules[0] edit covers both;
GF2 adds the exact formula and the ranking rule, GF7 adds the legend and the card format.

## GF8 (Major) — "identity" / persistence — RIGHT

`rules[1]` and `elephant.design` say ratings are "saved to each agent's identity" and
`elephant.gaps` says they "carry to a later table only if that table resumes the agent's earlier
session". Verified: `app.rs:426-429` defines an identity as its genesis **session** (profiles are
keyed by session, name held inside); `app.rs:430-443, 498-509` give the storage file; the core
reads profiles at `turn.rs:39-40, 521` only when an identity store is present. `element.md` never
defines "identity", never links `code.identity.agent`, and never gives the storage path.

**What should change:** define "identity" in `element.md` (the genesis session / its profile
file), link `code.identity.agent`, give the storage location `$ROUNDTABLE_HOME/identities/<session>.json`,
and state the persistence condition explicitly (a later table must resume the earlier session;
ratings are not attached to a bare name). Why: "saved to identity" is otherwise ambiguous and its
durability cannot be predicted. Merge with GF3 (which supplies who writes and where).

## GF9 (Major) — wants vs `rules[1]`: "results" — RIGHT

The `wants` entry for `code.manager.chat.group` says the element "Collects every agent's ratings
of the others and returns the results" (Intent `send_receive`), while `rules[1]` says agents
"receive the owner's results message". What "results" are (per-card scores, session point totals,
the ranking) and what goes to the manager versus to the agents is not stated in `element.md`.
Verified against the two quoted lines. In the code, "results" = `session_results.md` /
`session_rank.md` (ranking with per-seat points, card counts, and cumulative rating), sent to
seats, while ratings are also emitted as `roundtable.rating` events and written to identity
profiles — there is no in-process return value to the manager.

**What should change:** in `element.md`, define "results" as the session ranking message and
clarify the `wants` wording: it records a functional *want/intent* (`send_receive`), satisfied
through the event stream and identity profiles, not a literal return value to
`code.manager.chat.group`. State what agents receive (the ranking message) versus what the wider
system receives (rating events, persisted points). Why: the current wording implies two different
things called "results" with no definition.

## GF10 (Major) — "table" / endings / scope — RIGHT

`element.md` uses "table" throughout and says "When a table ends" without defining the term, the
end triggers, or whether the evaluator/chair take part. Verified against `element.md`: no such
definitions exist. The code shows only named, `Ready` seats are rated (`turn.rs:421-425, 438`),
so the evaluator/chair (not seats) are out of scope, and departed/non-answering seats are handled
as in GF1/GF5. The engine-level end triggers (`engine.rs:636-650, 791, 840, 903, 906`) are
**reported, not verified** but sit behind `start_rating`.

**What should change:** define "table" (the running Roundtable session with its seats), state what
ends one (chair End, round limit, sustained inactivity — per the engine), state that the rating
round covers the participating seats only (not the evaluator or chair), and describe departed and
non-answering agents. Why: these are preconditions the rule silently assumes. Merge the trigger
list with GF1 so it appears once.

## GF11 (Nit) — references / "owner" — RIGHT

`references` lists two bare paths with no note on what each file is; that `session_scoring.md` is
"the owner's scoring prompt" is only implied; "owner" (used in `rules`, `owner_statements`,
`elephant`) is never introduced. Verified against `element.md`.

**What should change:** annotate each reference (`session_scoring.md` = the scoring prompt sent to
agents; `docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md` = the owner-source record) and introduce
"owner" (the project author whose requirements/decisions the map records). Why: without it the
phrase "the owner's scoring prompt" is unresolvable. Together with the GF6 reclassification, this
item absorbs GF6's valid residue (the composite-resource label); the two should be one edit, not
two.

## GF12 (Nit) — owner_statements provenance — RIGHT

`owner_statements[0]` is the question "what about agent ratings at the end and saving the agents
rating". `element.md` gives no account of how the specific categories/weights (10/20/30/40, +5)
in `rules[0]` came from it. Verified: the categories derive from `session_scoring.md` (a
`references` entry) and, per `rules.rs:150`, "the owner's earlier system", not from that
statement.

**What should change:** add a short provenance note: the owner statement raised the feature; the
categories, weights, star scale, and bonus come from the referenced `session_scoring.md` / the
owner's earlier system. Why: it explains why the rule has those exact numbers and closes the
traceability gap. Keep it a note, not a rewrite of `owner_statements`.

---

## Consolidated fix plan (avoid duplicate edits)

All edits are to `element.md` unless noted; no rating-logic code change is warranted.

1. **`rules[0]` rewrite (GF1, GF2, GF7, GF10):** define "table" and its endings; state the round
   covers ready, named, remaining seats (not evaluator/chair); list skip conditions (fewer than
   two, forced ends) and no-retry on missing ratings; define the scorecard JSON shape, the 0–5
   star scale, the 10/20/30/40 weights as maxima, the weight/5 formula, the +5 boolean bonus and
   its criterion, silent zeros, and the 105 per-card cap.
2. **`rules[1]` + results definition (GF2, GF5, GF9):** describe the `score_received` receipt,
   the results message as a ranking by summed session points with `rating = prior + session`
   ("unscored" until rated), delivery to ready/named/idle seats and the end-when-sent condition,
   and clarify the manager "returns the results" want versus what agents receive.
3. **New "identity, storage & persistence" section (GF3, GF8):** the core emits
   `roundtable.rating` events and reads profiles; the web host writes
   `$ROUNDTABLE_HOME/identities/<session>.json` via `save_rating`; define identity (genesis
   session), link `code.identity.agent`, state the resume-session carry-over condition; correct
   `elephant.built` so it does not credit `turn.rs` with saving.
4. **New "failure modes" layer (GF4):** JSON brace-extraction, unreadable/non-object rejection,
   zero/multiple name matches, duplicate-name consequence.
5. **References, owner, provenance (GF11, GF12):** annotate references, introduce "owner", and
   record where the categories/weights came from. Note the first-turn `session_profile` line
    (GF5) as a related behaviour.
 6. **GF6 (partially right):** merged into item 5 — label `session_scoring.md` as a composite
    resource (owner notice + rubric + bonus + JSON format), do not claim verbatim owner text,
    keep the rubric. No code change; premise about the owner source stays flagged unverifiable.

## Observations raised during the roundtable (flagged, not GF verdicts)

Two points surfaced from other participants that are worth recording but are **outside** the
GF1–GF12 verdicts. They are marked as possibilities, not established defects, because their
execution depends on code not in this folder or on task scheduling.

- **Possible double-count of the cumulative rating (from `DeifiedArrow-notes.md` item 2).**
  `finish_ratings` reads the stored profile as `prior` and displays `prior.score + session_points`
  (`turn.rs:521-532`). But `save_rating` increments `profile["points"]` for every
  `roundtable.rating` event (`app.rs:500-508`), and those events are published during the round
  (`turn.rs:475-484`) on a bus drained by a separate host task (`app.rs:75-127`). If the host
  persists an early card before the last rater finishes, `prior.score` already contains
  current-session points, which are then added a second time in the displayed rating. This is a
  code-visible ordering hazard, not a measured execution trace; confirming it needs the bus/task
  scheduling detail. It is not among the review findings, so it should be a follow-up note, not a
  change to any GF decision.
- **GF9 wording caution (from `clarifications.TotalLogic.md` item 2).** Do not assert as verified
  that "`code.manager.chat.group` consumes the published events" — the manager's code is not in
  this `source/`. The safe statement, used above, names only this element's two outputs (published
  `RatingGiven` events and the per-seat `session_results` message) and leaves the manager's
  consumption to the manager element. (One other participant's `resolution.TotalLogic.md` GF9
  does say "the manager consumes the returned data"; that claim should be softened to match this
  caveat.)

## Note on the code vs the description

No finding identifies a defect in `rating_points`, `on_rating`, `finish_ratings`, or the host's
`save_rating`: the implementation is internally consistent (clamping, silent zeros, single-target
name matching, atomic profile writes, sum-based ranking all behave as the code comments say). The
reviewers' substantive points are that `element.md` is a high-level map that omits these details
and attributes saving to the wrong component. The right remedy is to enrich the description (and
fix `elephant.built`), not to change the rating code.

## DeifiedArrow — qualifications to the consolidated decision

The following points qualify the broad “description-only, no code defect” conclusion above.

- **GF4:** the corrected two-same-name example above is essential. The predicate `j != i`
  means exactly two same-named seats can manually rate one another. A third rater cannot
  distinguish them, and the automatic prompt omits same-named peers. To satisfy the existing
  “each agent rates every other” requirement for legal name collisions, use stable seat IDs as
  scorecard keys, show names alongside those IDs, and validate against the rater's eligible
  targets. Merely documenting the limitation does not fulfill that requirement. Rejected
  ambiguous cards produce notices; the rejection is not silent, although the final ranking
  shows a reduced received-card count.
- **GF5:** `check_results_done` (`turn.rs:568-570`) also waits while an eligible seat is in
  `Activity::Notified`. “Ends once all are sent” is incomplete: notification replies must
  settle. In addition, `results_sent` is set before `offer`, whose success is ignored
  (`556-557`), so attempted delivery is the verified contract, not guaranteed receipt.
- **GF6:** I disagree with a definitive “not right” verdict. The absent owner-source document
  prevents confirming or refuting the provenance comparison. A resource's use as the scoring
  prompt does not establish that its rubric was authored or approved by the owner. Qualify
  “owner's scoring prompt” as the implemented scoring resource pending inspection of the
  original. Retain the rubric: inaccurate attribution does not justify deleting instructions.
- **GF2:** the cumulative-profile ordering hazard recorded above directly qualifies the phrase
  “earlier profile score.” The code reads a live profile, not a pre-table snapshot. Capture
  the baseline before current-table rating events, or exclude this table's entries, to guarantee
  the stated cumulative result. A regression should let persistence consume an early card before
  the final rater completes; the displayed cumulative total must remain historical plus current
  points exactly once. This is a code recommendation supported by a possible ordering, not a
  claim that the failure was reproduced here.

I agree with naming only the verified outputs under GF9: per-card events and per-seat ranking
messages. No ranking-event publication or manager consumption is established by this snapshot.
The missing-source caveat at the start remains applicable to all decisions.
