## GF6 — (Nit, codebase-details, gaps)
> Not stated: tool activity sets worked_in_topic, which affects table ending and idle-topic
> warnings (engine.rs:368-372, 647, 672; turn.rs:399-407). The concurrent-edits gap from
> investigations is still open but missing from the elephant gaps.

**Decision: SPLIT — the `worked_in_topic`→table-ending half is RIGHT; the "idle-topic warnings"
half is RIGHT (verified from sibling `turn.rs`); the missing-gaps half is RIGHT. Resolves to
DESCRIPTION changes.**

Verified line by line:
- engine.rs:672 `self.worked_in_topic = true;` is set inside `on_tool` when `Activity::Floor`
  receives `ToolActivity` — i.e. ACP tool activity during a floor turn.
- engine.rs:368-372 `topic_had_input()` returns `self.worked_in_topic || <accepted Message with
  this topic's prefix>`.
- engine.rs:647 uses `topic_had_input()` to decide whether a no-round-limit table ends after
  two quiet rounds (`!self.topic_had_input()` → `start_rating()`).
So the claim "tool activity sets worked_in_topic, which affects table ending" is **correct and
verified**, and it is genuinely relevant to this element: it is the mechanism by which *file
work in the shared workspace counts as input* and keeps a table alive. That is exactly knowledge
the map should hold and currently does not.

- **`idle_topics` / idle-topic warnings**: `turn.rs` is not copied into this element's `source/`,
  so the prior version of this resolution called the flag dead state. **That inference was wrong.**
  `turn.rs` exists in the sibling element `code.gate.quality/source/crates/roundtable/src/turn.rs`
  (`:399-407`), and `change_topic` there reads and writes `idle_topics`:
  ```rust
  if accepted || self.worked_in_topic { self.idle_topics = 0; }
  else { self.idle_topics += 1; if self.idle_topics == 2 {
         self.notice("warn", "Two topics in a row ended with nothing accepted and no work..."); } }
  ```
  So the idle-topic warning **is** substantiated: it fires at two consecutive topics with no
  accepted message and no `worked_in_topic`, and it is governed by the same flag GF6's first half
  concerns. This half of GF6 is therefore RIGHT and should be recorded, not dropped. (The warning
  is gated on `topics_active()`, so it only applies when topics are on.)

- **Missing gap**: `investigations` (element.md:34-39) records the concurrent-edits gap;
  `elephant.gaps` (element.md:52-55) lists only "Files are not checked by JEV...". So the open
  gap is indeed not carried into `gaps`. Confirmed.

What to change (description):
- Add to `elephant.gaps` (or a knowledge note): "Tool (file) activity during a turn sets
  `worked_in_topic` (engine.rs:672); with no round limit this counts as topic input
  (`topic_had_input`, engine.rs:368-372) and can postpone the table ending (engine.rs:647)."
- Note the idle-topic warning: two topics in a row with no accepted message and no file work
  raise a warning (`turn.rs:399-407`) — verified from the sibling copy.
- Carry the concurrent-edits item from `investigations` into `elephant.gaps` so the open gap is
  not lost. Note that the copied code contains **no** locking/coordination mechanism (search for
  `lock`/`flock`/`conflict` finds only the unrelated `Mutex<Vec<Harness>>`), which confirms the

## GF7 — (Major, comprehension, Properties.uri, elephant.built)
> The document doesn't say who creates the table's workspace folder, how its path is chosen, or
> whether it is new or existing; the uri points only to a README section.

**Decision: RIGHT; resolves to a DESCRIPTION change. This is the highest-value comprehension fix.**

Verified: the element never states any of those three facts. The README `uri` (element.md:11)
cannot supply them. Meanwhile the answer **is** fully derivable from the copied code:
- **Who creates it:** `Table::start` (engine.rs:401-402) calls
  `std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.cfg.workspace)` — the engine creates it, best-effort, before
  any seat launches.
- **How the path is chosen:** it comes from `TableConfig.workspace` (config.rs:143), is
  canonicalized (engine.rs:403, fallback to the raw path on failure), assigned back to
  `cfg.workspace`, and published as `TableOpened.workspace` (engine.rs:411). `cfg.scope`
  (config.rs:146) is independent.
- **New or existing:** `create_dir_all` is idempotent — it creates the folder if absent and is a
  no-op if it already exists. So both; the map should say "created if missing, otherwise reused".

Why Major: this is the core "what the part does" knowledge for a *shared workspace* element, and
its absence is what makes `elephant.built` unfalsifiable. It also subsumes GF4's "path published"
and GF5's "code not named" points.

What to change (description): replace the single sentence in `elephant.built` with the three
facts above and add the implementing files to `references` (see GF5). Suggested wording:
"The engine creates `cfg.workspace` at table start with `create_dir_all` (so a pre-existing
folder is reused), canonicalizes it, and publishes the effective path in `TableOpened`. Every
seat's session opens with that path as cwd (engine.rs:401-440, 976-978)."

## GF8 — (Major, comprehension, elephant.sources)
> The convention 'extra detail goes in files named with the agent's name' is not explained: what
> extra detail is, and what rule it relieves. The owner's evaluation specification is not defined
> or linked.

**Decision: RIGHT (with a useful correction from the copied source); resolves to a DESCRIPTION
change.**

Verified: `element.md:49` cites `"owner's evaluation specification: extra detail goes in files
named with the agent's name"` as a source, but the element never explains it or links the spec.

source**, in `resources/roundtable_prompt.md:10`:
> "If you have sample code, diagrams, or additional details, write them to a file on disk whose
> filename includes your agent name, within `{{artifact_directory}}`. In your reply, explain the
> substantive point and what the artifact establishes. A file reference alone does not make the
> reasoning visible in the discussion."

That text answers both of the reviewers' questions:
- **What "extra detail" is:** sample code, diagrams, additional details that are too large or too
  incidental for the chat message.
- **What rule it relieves:** no evaluation exemption is established. Supporting material goes
  in files, but the prompt still requires the reply to explain the substantive point and what
  its artifact establishes. File placement does not make a bare-link reply sufficient or waive
  evaluation thresholds. The existing owner acceptance establishes that file contents are
  unjudged, not that the reply's reasoning requirements are relaxed.

What to change (description): in `elephant.sources`, replace the bare phrase with a real pointer
to `resources/roundtable_prompt.md:10` (and add that file to `references`), plus one sentence
explaining the convention: bulk/detail goes to an agent-named file in the shared folder; the chat
message keeps a short substantive explanation so the evaluator still has something to judge.
Define "owner's evaluation specification" as that prompt/thresholds, or link it; do not leave it
as an undefined proper noun.

This also gives GF11 its answer (see below).

roundtable.resolution:
# Resolution: discussion record (`data.log.discussion`)

Prepared by ExactTiger. This resolves the findings; it does not implement the proposed code changes.

## Basis and intended contract

The supplied source consists of `record.rs` and `events.rs`. References below are relative to `source/`. Claims about `turn.rs`, `engine.rs`, `app.rs`, `tables.rs`, ACP shutdown, and the historical audit cannot be independently checked here. Their absence limits verification; it does not make the reported problems false.

Keep the author's goal of a complete table audit, including participant prompts and replies. Correct the description of the current implementation: it is an append-only subscriber to the event bus, not an implemented event-sourced engine or a demonstrated source of prompt-builder state. Distinguish the desired contract from current coverage and failures. Fix loss and missing audit data in code rather than making silent loss the accepted contract.

The absence of prompt fields in `events.rs` alone does **not** prove prompts are absent from the record: the recorder consumes `bus::Envelope`, including events from other publishers, as its ACP/monitor routing explicitly anticipates. Conversely, a bus tap alone cannot prove that every prompt was received by an agent. Completeness requires evidence about all relevant publishers and the capture boundaries.

## Decisions by finding

### GF1 — Right about the responsibility mismatch; qualify the title

`record.rs:38–57` only opens and appends a file. It implements no history query or prompt-construction API. Change the wants/decision text to distinguish the prompt builder's need for accepted history and deferred notices from this component's duty to persist events for audit. Attribute the live context source to the engine/prompt builder after checking the cited, unavailable files. Do not add disk reads to the prompt path merely to make the old description true.

“Does not supply prompt content” concerns serving context to the builder; it does not establish that prompt text is never persisted. Check the ACP prompt event publishers separately before claiming existing prompt capture is absent or complete. Explain that distinction in the description.

### GF2 — Right: event sequence is not a canonical turn number

`record.rs:14` records an envelope `seq`; `FloorGiven` has `round`, and `Contribution` has an optional `id`. Pass, skip and failure events have no explicit turn identity (`events.rs:38–55`). Neither a bus event sequence, a round number, nor a contribution label is a canonical logical turn identifier. The particular `R{topic}-{n}` format and assignment of null IDs rely on the unavailable producer code.

Retain the decision's explicit requirement for canonical turn identity and change the producer/event schemas: allocate a table-wide, monotonic turn number once per scheduled seat opportunity, including opportunities that are skipped. Carry it on the floor/skip and associated outcome events, including accepted/rejected contributions, passes and failures. Preserve the same number through evaluation or background-work continuation of that opportunity; allocate a new number only for a new opportunity. Topic changes must not reset it. Keep contribution IDs and bus `seq` for their separate purposes. Define this behavior in the description so missing and repeated outcomes can be audited without guessing from event adjacency.

### GF3 — Right about source ownership and absent explicit counts

Remove “source for all three” from the current implementation description: this writer does not implement replay, distribution, or deferred-notice consumption. Record those operations as responsibilities of the live engine, with this component retaining the emitted evidence. Accepted text, `scores`, `reasons`, `limit` and `judged` do exist in `Contribution`; do not describe all outcome information as missing.

There are no explicit truncation counts in the supplied contribution or proposal schemas (`events.rs:39–59`). The reported rejection and 512-unit proposal behavior requires confirmation in `turn.rs`. Document over-limit rejection separately from text truncation: rejected text has not necessarily been shortened. For actual shortening, change the producing code to emit original length, retained length, measurement unit and limit, and preserve the original input or an explicitly linked capture if the complete-reply contract is to hold. Keep the delivered/retained text distinguishable from the original reply. A limit or a prose reason alone cannot establish how much was removed.

### GF4 — Right about the early boundary; routing needs qualification

`record.rs:51–53` exits immediately after attempting to append `roundtable.ended`. Consequently it cannot record any later shutdown events. The specific ordering of SessionClosed and HarnessExited is reported by the reviewer, not verified in this snapshot.

Change recorder lifecycle management to keep the subscription active through table-owned shutdown, then signal a terminal recording boundary after relevant publishers have finished, drain preceding events and await recorder completion. Merely deleting the break and waiting for a shared bus to close can leave a table recorder alive indefinitely. Document whether `roundtable.ended` means discussion ended or capture ended; they must not be conflated.

Filtering other tables and unrelated global events is correct. The problem is table-relevant events without routable identity, not that every event on a shared bus must be copied into every file. Require those publishers to supply a table identity or a supported harness identity. Identify genuinely unowned events as out of scope and surface unexpected attribution failures through diagnostics. Do not assign unknown events arbitrarily to a table.

### GF5 — Right; serialization failure is worse than the wording suggests

`record.rs:50` discards append errors. Initial directory/open errors are returned, but asynchronous failures are not; `spawn_recorder` returning `Ok(())` therefore does not establish recording success. Return an observable completion/error handle, propagate write failures to the table manager, and mark the audit incomplete when writing fails. Define and await the final persistence boundary; do not claim crash durability merely because an append succeeded.

`line()` substitutes JSON null on serialization failure (`record.rs:17`). **In the recorder, that line is then dropped:** `table_of(null)` returns `None`, so the filter at line 47 continues before `writeln!`. Thus the finding is correct about lost payloads, but its assertion that the recorder writes those failed events as `data:null` is inaccurate.

Change serialization handling to report an explicit error rather than silently substituting null. Preserve event name/sequence and independently available routing identity in failure diagnostics; record an attributable failure marker where possible. If table identity itself is unavailable, report the failure outside the per-table file and expose incomplete coverage rather than claiming a successful complete record. Serialization diagnostics cannot restore a payload that was never serialized.

### GF6 — Right; separate verified schema from reported integration

Expand the description with:

- One JSON object per line: `seq` is the bus envelope sequence, `at_ms` is the envelope timestamp in Unix milliseconds, `event` is its wire name, and `data` is its serialized payload. These are envelope fields, not a canonical turn schema. The timestamp currently defaults to zero if it predates the Unix epoch.
- Append mode, table filtering and lifecycle boundaries. Describe order as the order received by this tap; do not promise additional delivery or durability guarantees without inspecting the bus.
- Routing precedence: a string `data.table` wins; otherwise use the prefix before the first slash of a string `data.harness` or object `data.harness.id` (`record.rs:24–35`).
- Default file location, configuration override and actual readers, after checking their implementations.

The reviewer reports `<ROUNDTABLE_HOME|~/.roundtable>/tables/<id>/record.jsonl` and readers in `app.rs:279–341`. That is a concrete lead for the documentation update, but `spawn_recorder` accepts an arbitrary `path`, so this module does not establish that default or those readers. Avoid inventing reader behavior from line numbers alone.

### GF7 — Right: make the architectural roles explicit

Replace the inconsistent current-state claims with: “The discussion record persists table-attributable bus events for audit. The live engine maintains the state used to build participant deliveries; record replay is not implemented by this module. Complete prompt/reply capture is the intended coverage, subject to the documented producer and lifecycle gaps.” Verify live-state ownership against the cited engine code before treating that clause as independently confirmed.

Outcome events and prompt/reply events can coexist in one audit file; those are compatible scopes. The contradiction is assigning the file authority for live context without an implemented read/replay path, and describing desired completeness as already achieved. Do not introduce a second store or replay architecture solely to resolve the wording.

### GF8 — Right: define the local vocabulary

Add a short glossary or links to authoritative definitions:

- **Table:** one collaboration instance and the routing scope of a record file.
- **Seat:** a participant slot associated with a harness/session; distinguish the slot from the agent's display name.
- **Seat availability:** whether that slot can currently take a turn; identify which readiness, failure, departure and work events establish it rather than claiming a recorded boolean exists.
- **Topic:** the current subject within the continuing table objective; changing topic does not start a new table record.
- **Disposition:** the handling/outcome of a submission, including acceptance, evaluator rejection or limit rejection, and any deferred feedback.
- **Veto:** evaluator rejection of a contribution, with feedback held for its author's next delivery as described in the map.
- **JEV:** the evaluator responsible for contribution checks and recorded judging results; obtain its official expanded name and criteria from its own documentation rather than guessing the acronym.
- **Truncation:** removal of part of text, with the measured counts and unit distinguished from rejection for exceeding a limit.
- **Canonical turn number:** the table-wide opportunity identifier specified in GF2, explicitly marked as a required addition rather than an existing event field.

### GF9 — Right: rationale is not traceable

Replace the bare audit codes with a stable path/link to the audit and anchors for E05, E06 and D01–D05, plus a short statement of the relevant observed behavior. Define “turn-label drift” from that evidence (what identifier differed from what expected identifier). No audit is supplied here, so the historical claim cannot be verified. If the audit cannot be recovered, mark it as an unverified historical account and use the present source references for the current defect rationale; do not fabricate a link or a historical diagnosis.

### GF10 — Right; duplicate of the location portion of GF6

Resolve together with GF6. State that the application creates one file per table, give the configured/default directory once verified, and distinguish that application convention from `spawn_recorder`'s caller-supplied path. No independent recorder code change is needed for this documentation omission.

### GF11 — Right: make missing request capture explicit

Replace “request ... had to be rebuilt” with the precise missing artifact: according to the author's gap statement, an original JEV request was not captured and a later reconstruction was necessary. Link the reconstruction/incident if available and label reconstructed input as reconstructed, not as the exact original request.

Retain this as a current gap until verified fixed. To meet the complete audit goal, have the evaluator publisher emit the actual assembled request and corresponding response, correlated to table, seat, turn and evaluation attempt. Existing contribution scores/reasons are outcome summaries, not evidence of the full evaluator exchange. Document separately the verified lifecycle/write/serialization gaps (GF4–GF5) and any prompt publisher gaps found by inspection; do not assert that all other traffic is captured merely because only one historical omission was listed.

### GF12 — Right about missing map conventions; small documentation fix

Define or link `role`, `name_length`, and `Intent` in the functional map's shared schema. State the reference point for send/receive explicitly. In these wants entries, the apparent intended direction is that the prompt builder receives history and the manager sends outcomes; confirm that against the map convention. `name_length: 2` matches the two words in “discussion record,” but that observation is not an authoritative schema definition. The meaning of `SE` cannot be derived from these files. Do not invent its expansion or add map metadata to runtime events.

## Verification expected when the fixes are implemented

Check canonical turn correlation across rejection, pass, skip, failure, background work and topic changes; distinguish rejected over-limit text from actual shortening; exercise append and serialization failure reporting; and verify that shutdown events precede successful recorder completion without including another table's traffic. Inspect the missing publishers and readers before certifying prompt/evaluator capture or documenting application paths. This decision-only change requires no runtime test run.

---

## Addendum: net-new refinements from the roundtable discussion (GlowingMarten)

These complement, and do not replace, ExactTiger's decisions above. Verified against `record.rs` / `events.rs` in `source/`.

**GF5 — one clarification that strengthens ExactTiger's correction.** The finding claims unserializable payloads are "written as data:null." ExactTiger (line 45) correctly notes they are actually DROPPED: `line()` sets `data = null` (record.rs:17), then `table_of(&line["data"])` calls `data.get("table")` on a null value → `None` → `table_of` falls through to `harness_id` → also `None` → returns `None` → the filter at record.rs:47 `continue`s before `writeln!`. So the finding is right that payloads are LOST but wrong about the mechanism (not written as null, skipped). The fix must therefore emit an attributable failure marker OUTSIDE the routing filter, or the diagnostic itself will be dropped too. This is a real consequence: any fix that relies on the normal `line()` → `table_of` → `writeln!` path cannot record its own serialization failures.

**GF1 — the prompt-field argument cuts both ways.** ExactTiger (line 11) is right that `events.rs` having no prompt event does not PROVE prompts never reach the file, because `spawn_recorder` consumes a generic `bus::Envelope` from any publisher. But the reverse also holds: nothing in the shipped `record.rs`/`events.rs` demonstrates a prompt IS captured. So the honest description is "prompt/reply capture is the intended coverage, unverified" — which is exactly what ExactTiger proposes for GF7 (line 62). The `elephant.built` claim "including each prompt text" should be downgraded from asserted to intended until the ACP/harness publishers are inspected.

**GF2 — cheaper implementation path, consistent with ExactTiger's GF2.** ExactTiger asks for a table-wide monotonic turn allocated per scheduled seat opportunity. The shipped schema already provides `round: u64` on `FloorGiven` (events.rs:38) and `RoundClosed` (events.rs:56), and `index: u64` on `TopicChanged` (events.rs:59). So the code change should REUSE the existing round counter by propagating `round`/`turn` onto `Contribution`, `Passed`, `Skipped`, `TurnFailed`, rather than introducing a second competing counter. Note also the finding's "No canonical turn number exists" is loose: a round number DOES exist; the precise defect is that per-turn *outcome* events carry no turn/round identifier, so a stored outcome cannot be tied to its canonical turn from the recorded event alone. Finding still right in substance.

**GF4 — the boundary is a design choice, not only a bug.** The `break` at record.rs:51–53 is a deliberate "capture only the active table lifecycle" boundary. The resolution is a choice, and the description must be updated either way: (a) document that the record intentionally stops at `roundtable.ended` and drop "every event", or (b) extend through teardown. ExactTiger recommends (b) with proper lifecycle/drain handling (line 37) — agreed, but note the ambiguity itself, not merely the `break`, is the defect. Also GF10 is a strict subset of GF6 (both concern the undocumented path/location); resolve them together, not as independent fixes.

**GF8 — prefer cross-references over a duplicated glossary.** Most undefined terms are defined in sibling map elements: JEV in `code.gate.quality`, seat/roster in `code.roster.participant`, topic in `code.selector.topic`, veto/deferred feedback in README §4.6 (already in `references`). A glossary that re-defines them will drift. Link to those elements; give local one-line definitions only for record-specific terms (`canonical turn number`, `table`, `disposition`, `truncation`). This is cheaper and keeps one source of truth.

**GF11 — partly misframed on "contradiction."** ExactTiger marks GF11 flatly "Right." It is right about vagueness, but the charge that the note "contradicts the 'complete record' claim" is weak: the elephant layer has a dedicated `gaps` field whose entire purpose is to acknowledge known absences, so a note in `gaps` is the author ADMITTING incompleteness, not contradicting the design goal. Also the gap IS named ("JEV's requests are not recorded"), so "without saying what else is missing" overstates — it is named, just not specified. Verdict: RIGHT on vagueness, PARTLY MISFRAMED on contradiction. Net: 11 of 12 findings fully right; GF11 qualified. (The GF5 mechanism correction above likewise means GF5 is right in substance, wrong in one detail.)

**Priority of work** (from GlowingMarten's independent verdicts, consistent with ExactTiger's):
1. Description reconciliation — record is a write-only, append-only bus-tap audit trail, NOT the distribution/disposition/context source (GF1, GF3, GF7). Highest value, single edit to `decisions` + `wants` + `elephant.built`.
2. Code fixes that a functional `want` or the design goal genuinely require: canonical turn identity (GF2), lossless lifecycle/routing/write/serialization handling (GF4, GF5), JEV-request capture (GF11).
3. Documentation: Storage/Representation section (GF6, GF10), glossary/cross-refs (GF8), linked audit evidence (GF9), map-schema note (GF12).

Auditability note: findings citing `turn.rs`, `engine.rs`, `app.rs`, `tables.rs`, `harness.rs` cite files NOT in this element's `source/` folder (only `record.rs`, `events.rs` are present). Those line-level citations are not independently checkable here; every verdict above is grounded in the two shipped files and the description.

roundtable.resolution:
# Resolution — Participant System Prompt

Basis: the description in `element.md` and the code copied in `source/` (two prompt text files, `prompts.rs`, `turn.rs`). Each decision below states: what the code actually does in plain operational terms, whether the finding is right, exactly what should change (description or code), why it matters, and how to check the claim (a specific file/line or a search a reader can repeat). The findings also cite `engine.rs`, `config.rs` and `acp-host events.rs`. These are not in this element's `source/`, but byte-congruent copies exist in sibling element folders of the same codebase (e.g. `collection.workspace.shared/source/crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs`, `code.identity.agent/.../config.rs`), and the cited line numbers were checked against them (see the Addendum). Claims resting on those files are therefore verified, not assumed; `source/`-only checks are noted as such where they matter.

## GF1 — Upheld (Major)
**What happens in the code:** When a seat's first prompt of any kind is built, `turn_prompt` (`turn.rs`) puts the full prompt (outer template with the inner prompt inside it) in front of that turn's content, because a flag on the seat (`seat.first`) is still set. After that prompt is sent, `commit` clears the flag, so no later prompt gets the full template again. A discussion turn is only one kind of prompt; review, topic-proposal and rating prompts also count as "first" if they happen to be first.
**Decision:** the finding is right. The description's "first turn of each session" is wrong in a way that matters: a reader would expect the full template only on the first discussion turn and would misjudge what a seat that is first asked a review or rating prompt actually receives.
**Change (description only):** replace "first turn of each session" with "first prompt of any kind for that seat (while its `first` flag is set)".
**Check:** read `turn_prompt`'s `if seat.first` branch and `commit` setting `first = false`. The resumed-session half of the finding is confirmed by the sibling `engine.rs`/`config.rs` copies (Addendum): `resume_session` only selects the harness session open path (`engine.rs:976-977`), `first` is initialized `true` for every seat at `Table::new` (`engine.rs:324`) and cleared only by `commit`, so a resumed seat retains `first == true` and receives the full template again.

## GF2 — Upheld (Major)
**What happens in the code** (`prompts.rs` `roundtable_prompt`, `turn.rs` `turn_prompt`):
- `{{AgentName}}` → the seat's human name if it has one, otherwise its seat label.
- `{{roundtable_subject}}` → the current topic text returned by `self.topic()`, initially the configured nonblank topic or otherwise the objective (sibling `collection.workspace.shared/source/crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs:306`).
- `{{custom_roundtable_prompt}}` → the second owner text, with the objective substituted into its own placeholder.
- `{{artifact_directory}}` → the configured workspace folder path as text. Sibling `engine.rs:402–404` creates the directory, attempts canonicalization, falls back to the original path on failure, and writes the result into `cfg.workspace`. Thus “canonical workspace” describes the successful case, not an unconditional guarantee.
- `{{delivery_json}}` → the turn's content parts joined by blank lines. Despite the name, this is plain text, not structured data.
**Decision:** the finding is right. Without this table, nobody can predict what any given seat reads, because five different values are substituted into one template.
**Change (description only):** add this table to the element and flag `delivery_json` as a plain-text misnomer.
**Check:** the five substitutions are each one line in `prompts.rs` / `turn.rs`; no other code fills them.

Also document the inner template's `{{roundtable_prompt}}` → `cfg.objective` substitution (`prompts.rs:12–14`). The same name here denotes the objective, not the outer template.

## GF3 — Upheld (Major)
**What happens in the code:** The outer template always contains a paragraph saying the seat's message is scored by an automated checker (JEV) and can be rejected. But in `submit` (`turn.rs`), a message is instead shared with everyone without any checking in three cases: judging is switched off; the checker has no API key; the checker errors or cannot fit the message. In those cases the message still reaches the other seats, with an internal note saying it was unjudged.
**Decision:** the finding is right. The first prompt tells every seat something that is not always true, so seats may write defensively or blame themselves for rejections that cannot happen.
**Change (description only; code change is the owner's call):** record as a gap that the prompt always promises JEV evaluation while the code shares messages unjudged in the three cases above. Do not change the prompt text unilaterally: both prompt texts are the owner's, kept verbatim by design (`prompts.rs` header comment).
**Check:** `turn.rs` branches `if !self.judging`, `if !self.jev.configured()`, and the checker-error branch each call the same "accept unjudged" path.

The inner `participant_prompt.md:15` makes the same unconditional evaluation promise; record the gap against both templates. “Unjudged” does not bypass length enforcement (`turn.rs:125–145`), and the delivery shown to peers does not itself include the internal unjudged note.

## GF4 — Upheld (Major)
**What happens on the first prompt, in order** (`turn.rs` `turn_prompt`): (1) a round line like "Round 2 of 5" — discussion prompts only; (2) if the seat is a returning identity with past ratings, its profile score, rating count and session count; (3) any pending notices for that seat — discussion prompts only; (4) on later prompts, a "Current topic: …" line when topics are enabled and the topic changed since the seat last spoke; (5) every other seat's accepted messages and any chair messages the seat has not yet seen, each prefixed with an ID or "Chair:"; (6) any special request attached to this prompt (review, topic proposal, or rating request).
**Decision:** the finding is right. This is the complete list of what a seat reads on its first prompt; omitting it makes the element unusable for judging whether seats have what they need.
**Change (description only):** document items (1)–(6) above, in that order.
**Check:** each item is a separate `parts.push(...)` in `turn_prompt`.

## GF5 — Upheld (Nit)
**What happens in the code:** The full template is built as an ordinary string and sent as the content of the seat's prompt. There is no code anywhere in `source/` that passes it through an optional harness extension field (the investigation's example was a `_meta.systemPrompt` field that some agent harnesses accept).
**Decision:** the finding is right but small: the investigation describes an option the code never uses, so a reader cannot tell what was actually chosen.
**Change (description only):** reword the investigation to state the chosen path: "delivered as prompt content; the optional harness-extension path is not implemented." Independently checked sibling `collection.workspace.shared/source/crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs:597–601` builds the text, passes it to `harness.prompt`, then commits after success. The broader search reported below supports the absence of the alternative path; the four local files alone would not establish that negative.
**Check:** search `source/` for `_meta` or `systemPrompt` — zero hits.

## GF6 — Upheld in full (Nit)
**Naming part — right.** The element is called "Participant System Prompt" but its single file pointer (`uri`) is `resources/roundtable_prompt.md`, which is the *other* owner text. A reader following the pointer gets a different file than the name promises.
**Gap-wording part — right.** The finding proposes replacing the existing gap ("Nothing tells an agent that its reply is the message the others receive") with "only the final block after the last tool call becomes the message." The sibling `engine.rs:691-699` confirms this: `// gate: RT-G09 only the text after the last tool call becomes the message ... the turn's final message, not its narration before tool calls`, and `resolve_reply(i, &event.final_message, ...)` consumes that final text. `acp-host/events.rs:147-149` is likewise not in this folder, but the engine-side comment and the `final_message` field are direct evidence.
**Change (description only):** fix the name/pointer mismatch (see GF7); adopt the more precise gap wording so the description matches the reply-resolution mechanism.
**Check:** sibling `engine.rs:691-699` (RT-G09 comment + `event.final_message`); `turn.rs` `resolve_reply` receives that text as the seat's message.

## GF7 — Upheld (Major)
**What the element actually covers:** a composition of two owner texts. The outer template (`roundtable_prompt.md`) is sent once per seat; the inner text (`participant_prompt.md`) is inserted into it at the `{{custom_roundtable_prompt}}` slot. Neither text alone is the element.
**Decision:** the finding is right. Because the element never says which of the three (outer, inner, composition) it is, every other statement in it — including the name in GF6 — is ambiguous.
**Change (description only):** add one sentence: "This element covers the composition of the two owner prompt texts; `uri` points at the outer template as the composition's entry point." No code change. The URI need not change once scope is explicit; the inner prompt is actually rendered before the outer one in `turn_prompt`. Explain that “System Prompt” is a display name, not a claim about the ACP transport role.
**Check:** `turn_prompt` builds `custom = prompts::participant_prompt(...)` and passes it into `prompts::roundtable_prompt(...)` as one string.

## GF8 — Upheld (Major)
**The problem:** the gap "'Topics may change' is not true while topics are off" uses a switch ("topics") that the element never defines: what it does (lets the group move to new subjects), who turns it on (the chair/table configuration), and whether it is on by default.
**Decision:** the finding is right. A gap statement that depends on an undefined switch cannot be acted on.
**Change (description only):** add one defining sentence — what topics mode is, who sets it, and its default — or rephrase the gap without the term.
**Check:** the words "topics" appear in `element.md` only inside that one gap; no definition exists anywhere in the element.

The sibling `collection.workspace.shared/source/crates/roundtable/src/config.rs:150–153` defines `TableConfig.topics` with `#[serde(default)]`, confirming it is off by default. Its comment identifies the next-topic poll and `advance` tool as the controlled functions. Sibling `engine.rs:374–378` additionally requires judging and a configured evaluator key. Document these actual controls and conditions. “Topics may change” expresses possibility, so topics being off is not a strict contradiction; the actionable gap is missing mode awareness.

## GF9 — Upheld (Major)
**What happens in the code:** The prompt texts contain no mention of reply length limits (the owner deleted those lines). Limits are instead enforced after the fact: a contribution longer than an applicable seat character limit is blocked from group delivery (`turn.rs` `submit`), and on that seat's next prompt it receives a notice stating the length and the limit, plus any rejection feedback. So seats *are* told about limits, but only reactively, after violating them.
**Decision:** the finding is right. The decision record says the lines were deleted without saying whether anything replaced them; a reader would reasonably conclude seats are never told, which is false.
**Change (description only):** append to the decision: "Contribution limits are not stated in the common templates; when a limit applies, over-limit contributions are blocked in full, with feedback queued for the next discussion prompt." Sibling `code.rating.peer/source/crates/roundtable/resources/feedback/too_long.md` explicitly says the message was not shared and gives its length and limit. Topic proposals are different: `prompts.rs:85–86` announces their limit and `turn.rs:320–324` truncates them. Describe the deleted sentences' historical purpose only from an available original; do not reconstruct what the deleted credit sentence said.
**Check:** `turn.rs` `submit` blocks over-limit replies and pushes a `too_long` notice onto the seat's pending notices; `turn_prompt` delivers those notices on the next discussion prompt.

Qualification from sibling `collection.workspace.shared/source/crates/roundtable/src/config.rs:154–158`: the base contribution allowance is optional and defaults to no limit. The chair sets it. The missing advance guidance matters when a limit applies; the default does not impose a hidden finite base allowance.

## GF10 — Upheld (Nit)
**The problem:** the investigation presents two delivery routes (prompt content vs. harness extension) without saying which one the code uses, and says nothing about what happens if a session is restarted.
**Decision:** the finding is right, and its answer is now known from GF5: the code always uses prompt content. Restart behaviour is the GF1 question, and it is confirmed by the sibling `engine.rs`/`config.rs` (Addendum): `resume_session` only selects the harness open path and never resets `first`, which stays `true` from `Table::new` until `commit`, so a resumed seat receives the full template again.
**Change (description only):** state the chosen route (per GF5) and the restart behaviour: a resumed session keeps `seat.first == true` (Addendum, `engine.rs:324,976-977`), so the full template is sent again.
**Check:** GF5's search (no `_meta` usage anywhere in the egm tree; `session/new` appears only for MCP/auth in `acp-host/harness.rs`) plus GF1's `seat.first` logic in `source/` and the sibling `engine.rs`.

## GF11 — Upheld (Nit)
**The problem:** the properties block says `name_length: 2` for a three-word name, and the field is defined nowhere — so the reader cannot tell whether 2 is a mistake or means something else (for example, the number of prompt texts the element covers, which genuinely is 2).
**Decision:** the finding is right as far as it goes: the value is at minimum unexplained.
**Change (description only):** link or define the authoritative map schema, then validate the value. Change it to 3 only if the schema defines word count. Do not invent “number of owner prompt texts covered” as a definition merely because there are two texts. No supplied source reads this field; the rest of the map tooling is absent.
**Check:** `name: "Participant System Prompt"` = 3 words; no definition of `name_length` exists in `element.md`. Cross-element comparison confirms it is NOT a word count: `code.manager.chat.group` name "Roundtable" (1 word) has `name_length: 3`, `code.builder.prompt` name "participant turn prompt" (3 words) has `name_length: 2`, `code.identity.agent` "agent genesis names" (3 words) has 3, `downstream.chair` "user" (1 word) has 1. So changing this value to 3 would be a guess; the schema must be consulted.

## GF12 — Upheld (Nit)
**The problem, in plain terms:** the element uses several technical terms without explaining them for a reader who only has this document: the agent-protocol name (ACP), "harness" (the program that runs/pass-throughs a seat's agent), the session/prompt and session/new message types, the optional extension field name, "evaluation specification" (the owner's scoring document), and the map's own field labels `role` and `Intent`.
**Decision:** the finding is right from the standpoint of a reader of this element alone. Note the practical consequence is limited: `role` and `Intent` are map-wide labels presumably defined once for the whole map, so the fix needed *here* is only for the integration terms GF5/GF10 use.
**Change (description only):** add a short glossary for the integration terms, or expand each use into a plain sentence (e.g. "the program that runs the agent" instead of "harness").
**Check:** each term appears in `element.md` with no definition in the same document.

## Summary
- Upheld fully: GF1, GF2, GF3, GF4, GF5, GF6, GF7, GF8, GF9, GF10, GF11, GF12. (GF6's naming and its "final block after the last tool call" gap wording are both confirmed by the sibling `engine.rs:691-699`; see the qualifiers in CarnalChange's note below — that text is only a *candidate* message, still subject to classification, the length block and JEV veto, and ratings use a separate path.)
- Rejected outright: none.
- Code changes required: none to runtime behaviour or the owner's verbatim prompt texts. Every upheld finding is a description change. Comment-only corrections (CarnalChange, below) are appropriate. The only candidate behavioural change (GF3: making the evaluation paragraph conditional) edits an owner's verbatim text and is the owner's explicit call.
- Claims that cite `engine.rs` / `config.rs` / `acp-host events.rs` (GF1 resume, GF2 objective-default, GF6 final-block, GF8 topics-default, GF5/GF10 delivery path) are **verified** against congruent copies in sibling element folders; none are left unverified. The one field that is genuinely undefined is `name_length` (GF11): cross-element data shows it is not a word count, so its value cannot be "fixed to 3" without the map schema.

## CarnalChange — implementation-comment corrections and output-boundary qualification

The findings also justify small source-comment corrections, without changing owner templates or runtime behavior. `turn.rs:124` says “Truncate, then judge” although `submit` blocks contributions; `turn.rs:22–25` and the `prompts.rs` module header refer to a default characters line that `turn_prompt` never assembles. Update those comments to describe current behavior. Thus the summary's “no code changes” means no runtime changes; comment fixes remain appropriate.

For GF6, the verified final-block wording must describe a **candidate** contribution. `resolve_reply` still classifies it, `submit` can block it, and judging can veto it. Special prompts such as ratings use separate handling. It would be incorrect to state that every final assistant block necessarily becomes a message shared with the group. The name/URI ambiguity is resolved by documenting composition, not by treating differently named files as inherently erroneous.

For GF12, define ACP as Agent Client Protocol, `session/new` as session creation, and `session/prompt` as submitting content to a session; identify the actual owner evaluation document/version when available. Link the schema for `role`, `Intent`, and `name_length`; their meanings should not be guessed from labels. See `CarnalChange-evidence.md` for independently checked source locations.

## Addendum (UnseenBobcat): resolved sub-claims GF1 resume, GF2 default-topic, GF6 final-block

The two sub-claims above were flagged unverifiable because `engine.rs`/`config.rs`
are not in `source/`. They are verifiable: the same `crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs`
and `config.rs` are copied into sibling element folders in this workspace (e.g.
`collection.workspace.shared/source/crates/roundtable/src/`). The findings cite
these exact paths; all map elements reference the same codebase. Observed lines:

- **GF2 default-topic** — `engine.rs:306`:
  `let topic = cfg.topic.clone().filter(|t| !t.trim().is_empty()).unwrap_or_else(|| cfg.objective.clone());`
  Topic falls back to the objective. Confirms GF2's "roundtable_subject = topic,
  defaulting to the objective."
- **GF1 resume** — `config.rs:23-28` defines `resume_session: Option<String>`;
  `engine.rs:976-977`:
  `let opened = match &seat.resume_session { Some(id) => harness.resume_session(workspace, id, servers).await, None => harness.open_session(workspace, servers).await };`
  Resume only chooses the harness session; it does not touch the seat's `first`
  flag (set `true` for every seat in `Table::new`, `engine.rs:324`, cleared only
  by `commit`). So a resumed seat still has `first==true` and receives the full
  roundtable prompt again. Confirms GF1's "resumed sessions receive it again."
- **GF6 final-block** — `engine.rs:691-695`:
  "gate: RT-G09 only the text after the last tool call becomes the message. The
  agent's message is what it says once it has finished: the turn's final message,
  not its narration before tool calls." Confirms GF6's proposed gap wording.
- **GF8 topics mode** — `engine.rs:374-378`: topics are "a table setting, off by
  default," active only when `cfg.topics && self.judging && self.jev.configured()`.

Recommended action: adopt GF1's resume half and GF6's replacement wording, and
record GF2's default-topic line as verified. This changes the summary to: GF6
upheld in full (naming and wording), GF1 upheld including resume. It does not
change any code action; all fixes remain description changes in `element.md`.
Caveat (UnseenBobcat): byte-identity between sibling copies was inferred from the
shared, cited paths. This caveat is now removed (see the checksum addendum below).

## Addendum (RusticEquity): byte-identity of sibling copies — closes the "unverifiable" objection

AnalogCarbine's stated condition for flipping GF1's resume half and GF6's wording
was "if the resume code does re-set the flag and the reply handling does take only
the final text block." Both are confirmed below. The remaining worry — that sibling
copies might differ from the codebase the reviewers cited — is settled by checksum:

- `md5sum` of every `crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs` in the egm tree (4 copies:
  `code.manager.chat.group`, `code.quota.character`, `code.server.tool`,
  `collection.workspace.shared`) = `93c53f8c13f5a6a8cce054977e8f46ee` — identical.
- `md5sum` of every `crates/roundtable/src/config.rs` (4 copies:
  `code.identity.agent`, `code.quota.character`, `code.roster.participant`,
  `collection.workspace.shared`) = `2b11ea2f26e6dbb295b5e9cec553b475` — identical.
- The canonical `collection.workspace.shared/.../engine.rs` is 997 lines; the exact
  cited lines read: 306 topic→objective fallback; 324 `first: true`; 374-378
  topics off by default / `topics_active()`; 599 `harness.prompt(&session, text)`
  (prompt-content delivery, no `_meta.systemPrompt`); 691-699 RT-G09 final-block
  with `resolve_reply(i, &event.final_message, false)`; 976-977 resume only selects
  the harness open path.

Reproduce with:
`find /home/rich/roundtable-runs/egm -name engine.rs -path '*/roundtable/src/*' -exec md5sum {} \; | sort`
and the same for `config.rs`, then `nl -ba <canonical> | sed -n '306p;324p;374,378p;599p;691,699p;976,977p'`.

Conclusion: the four sub-claims (GF1 resume, GF2 objective-default, GF6 final-block,
GF8 topics-default) are verified against a single byte-identical codebase shared by
all map elements; the "unverifiable" framing is a false negative and is withdrawn.
A repo-wide search confirms zero `_meta` / `_meta.systemPrompt` / `systemPrompt`
occurrences (only `session/new` for MCP/auth in `acp-host/harness.rs`), so GF5/GF10's
"no harness-extension path" is verified, not merely inferred from a 4-file `source/`.
All fixes remain description changes in `element.md`; no code or owner-template edits.

# Resolution of findings for `downstream.chair` (`user`)

Prepared by TunedMantis. These are decisions and proposed changes; no implementation changes are claimed.

Evidence scope: the supplied snapshot contains only `crates/roundtable-web/assets/index.html`, `crates/roundtable-web/src/app.rs`, and `crates/roundtable-web/src/tables.rs`, all beneath `source/`. References below use those paths relative to `source/`. The reviewers' cited `engine.rs`, `turn.rs`, `events.rs`, `config.rs`, README, and Intake specification are absent. Claims depending on those files are identified as reviewer-reported rather than independently verified.

## GF1 — Accept: contribution scores are not displayed

`index.html:234` retains `d.scores`, but `renderItem` at lines 339–355 never renders them. Rejections display `reasons` and a tooltip containing `note`; neither provides the complete evaluation. Peer ratings are rendered separately at lines 242–243 and 251, so the finding concerns contribution evaluations, not a total absence of numerical scores.

Change the code to render the evaluation supplied with each judged contribution, accepted or rejected, with labeled checks/scores and any available explanation. Preserve the explicit unjudged state and do not fabricate scores for missing evaluations. If rejected evaluations are reduced to reason strings upstream, extend the event payload using the evaluator's actual schema; that upstream reduction is reported by the reviewer but cannot be checked here. Record the missing contribution-score display in `elephant.gaps` until implemented. The author's explicit visibility claim warrants a fix rather than simply deleting the promised feature.

## GF2 — Accept the overpromise; qualify the word “contradicts”

A want can describe an aspiration, but this want's function reads as a guarantee of actual behavior. The page defaults to ten rounds and topics unchecked (`index.html:139–140`); the request type defaults topics to false and documents ten rounds (`tables.rs:29–34`). Its round default delegates to a core constant whose definition is absent. The two-unproductive-round termination rule is reviewer-reported from the absent engine.

Change the description to: “Runs a turn-based discussion among heterogeneous agents sharing a workspace, with optional judging and topic progression, subject to configured limits and chair commands, to help produce the requested deliverable.” Document ten-round and topics-off defaults and the reported unproductive-round stopping rule, with its exact applicability checked against the engine before publishing it as independently verified behavior. Do not remove useful limits or enable topics merely to match the old prose. Ending a run does not prove a deliverable exists; see GF12.

## GF3 — Accept the ambiguity; preserve graceful ending

An End control exists and dispatches `Command::End` (`index.html:406`; `tables.rs:165`). Thus `elephant.built` is not false merely because ending takes a rating phase. However, the confirmation mentions shutting down every harness without explaining the intervening phase or the second-click behavior. Rating events are visibly supported (`index.html:242–243`); the first-End/second-End engine semantics are reviewer-reported, not independently verified here.

Describe the reported contract explicitly: first End requests the closing rating phase, after which the table shuts down; another End during closing stops immediately. Change the confirmation to explain that sequence. Have the UI track the engine's closing state and label the available action accordingly, such as “Stop now” during closing, rather than repeating the initial confirmation. Keep the engine's graceful behavior unless a separate requirement calls for immediate cancellation.

## GF4 — Accept as documentation coverage, not missing implementation

The omitted features are present: explicit or proposed next topics (`index.html:405`), judging toggle (407), OpenRouter settings (`app.rs:230–243`), stored-table replay (`app.rs:279–341`; `index.html:371–401`), received prompts (255, 321–331), and identity/session selection (412–457; `tables.rs:127–128`).

Expand the description with a compact account of these chair capabilities. Explain that replay reads a record rather than restarting a table, and that identity resume requests an earlier session from its harness rather than guaranteeing every harness can resume it. Mention that the key is held in memory and settings changes are forwarded to active tables' JEV instances. Topic progression and judging should state their configuration/key dependencies; the form already warns that absent an OpenRouter key, contributions are shared unjudged (`index.html:136`). No new controls are needed to resolve these omissions. Calling every omitted secondary feature Major overstates the implementation impact.

## GF5 — Accept: access prerequisites belong in the description

All registered `/api` routes use chair authentication (`app.rs:143–154, 192–198`), and the outer router checks Host and any supplied Origin (160, 170–183). The page itself at `/` is not behind chair-token authentication. The browser extracts the fragment token into tab session storage, removes the fragment, uses Bearer authentication for fetch, and supplies a token query parameter for the event stream (`index.html:164–169, 508`). The middleware actually accepts a query token for any API route, though the page uses it for the stream.

Document opening the startup-provided authenticated link, keeping the chair credential private, and using a server address accepted by these checks. State that reading/controlling the API needs the credential and participant tools use separate authorization. Preserve the protection. The page itself instructs use of the startup link (468, 505–506); the startup code printing that link is absent.

## GF6 — Partly accept; separate the four claims

- **`d.truncated`:** line 234 copies it, but the supplied renderer never uses it. Remove this dead client property unless an actual event contract and display requirement justify it. The claim that `Contribution` lacks the field depends on absent `events.rs`; this is not evidence of a current truncation-display failure.
- **512 default:** line 177 initializes temporary client state to 512, but `roundtable.opened` replaces it with `d.base_allowance` and updates existing seats (218); floor events also supply allowances (227). The creation form sends null for an empty limit (137, 486), matching `tables.rs:23–25`. Reject the implication that ordinary new tables are constrained to 512 characters. This also holds on replay: `openPast` (`index.html:391–401`) re-applies the recorded `roundtable.opened` event, whose unconditional `t.base = d.base_allowance` (`index.html:218`) overwrites the 512 default before any seat card renders, so a replayed no-limit table correctly shows "no length limit" (`index.html:317`). `history_list`'s summary lacking `base_allowance` (`app.rs:289`) is irrelevant — that summary feeds only the Past-tables list, not seat cards. No code change needed; the 512 is an inert placeholder.
- **Hold:** accept the need to document that it pauses scheduling new turns while ongoing work can continue, based on the reviewer's engine account. The supplied web code proves command dispatch, not cancellation semantics. “Hold” should not imply interrupting active agent work.
- **Empty gaps:** accept that confirmed mismatches such as GF1 belong there. An omitted description of an already implemented feature is fixed in the description, not recorded as a missing feature. Do not list all review comments indiscriminately as product gaps.

## GF7 — Accept the need to reconcile the accounts

“Observation-only” is a historical audit characterization, whereas the owner's later account explicitly intends interaction. Current source confirms guidance, hold/resume, advance, judging and end commands (`tables.rs:157–165`). There is no basis for restricting the current chair to observation to preserve the older wording.

Amend the decision to date and delimit the earlier audit: it described an observation-only chair in that audit's scope; the current chair can interact through the implemented controls. If that historical limitation cannot be substantiated from the audit, remove it as supporting evidence for current behavior. Keep the decision's useful definition of the chair as the person convening the table.

## GF8 — Accept: map terminology lacks a local explanation

Explain that `downstream.chair` is the stable map address and `user` is its human-facing alias; they need not be identical. Define the chair's responsibilities in ordinary language beside the role metadata. Link and summarize the authoritative meaning of `CQU` and the relevant Intake 3.1 naming rule before retaining the claim that `user` is invalid in that role. Neither authority is supplied, so inventing an acronym expansion or renaming the element based on the unsupported rule would be unjustified. If no authoritative definition is available, remove the unexplained rule claim and retain an explicit plain-language role description.

## GF9 — Accept the description omission; reject a missing-feature inference

The chair already enters the objective and selects seats, harnesses/custom commands and models in the New table dialog (`index.html:129–145, 409–457`). Submission includes objective and seats (484–488), and the server turns them into table configuration (`tables.rs:94–144`).

Add these setup capabilities to `elephant.built`: “The chair enters an objective and shared workspace and selects participants by seat, harness and optional model or resumable identity.” No implementation work or feature-gap entry is justified for objective/participant selection. The separate score-display gap still needs recording.

## GF10 — Accept: guidance delivery needs a contract

The page says guidance goes to every participant at its next turn (`index.html:115, 296`), posts a guidance command (402), and renders chair events separately from contribution events (248, 356). `tables.rs:162` maps nonblank guidance directly to `Command::Guidance`. This supports describing guidance as chair input rather than an ordinary participant contribution.

Document the recipients and deferred delivery: guidance is intended for all participants on their next turns, not injected into a prompt already in progress. State whether it bypasses JEV contribution judging. The separate web command path is consistent with bypass, but cannot establish the engine's judging behavior; verify that explicit clause in the missing command handler. Also specify retention across subsequent turns from that handler rather than assuming guidance is delivered only once or forever.

## GF11 — Accept: add access instructions and a short glossary

`app.rs:156, 164–165` serves the page at `/` through the supplied HTTP listener. Document opening the server's printed link at its configured HTTP address, including the chair token as described in GF5. Do not invent a default port or bind address: the executable selecting them is absent.

Define a table as one discussion run with an objective, configured participants and shared workspace; a rejection/veto as a participant contribution withheld from the group by evaluation while visible to the chair; and JEV as the contribution evaluator. Verify any acronym expansion against project documentation before adding it. These changes make the description understandable without requiring knowledge of internal labels.

## GF12 — Accept: stopping and acceptance are distinct

Neither the supplied API nor page provides a deliverable-acceptance command or a proof that work exists when a table ends. The chair requests a substantive deliverable and assesses whether it satisfies the objective; that acceptance responsibility should be stated as the intended human workflow, not asserted as an implemented completion detector.

Replace “until the work is produced” as proposed in GF2. Say explicitly that chair-requested termination, configured limits, and engine stopping rules can end a run without the chair accepting the deliverable. Evaluation scores and participant ratings judge contributions or participants; they do not establish deliverable acceptance. No new automatic completion mechanism is required by this element's stated design.

# ACP harness — review resolutions

Prepared by GammaLiquid from `element.md` and the supplied source snapshot; augmented by SternSalmon (see `SternSalmon-resolution.md`).

The snapshot contains only `source/crates/acp-host/src/launch.rs`. References below use its line numbers. The web catalog, OpenRouter adapter, RPC client, design documents, registry-source audit, and recorded runs are absent. A finding can correctly identify missing documentation without its underlying runtime claims being independently verified here. No finding establishes a code defect that requires changing the supplied launcher.

## GF1 — OpenRouter harness omitted

**Decision: Accept the documentation concern provisionally; the specific implementation claims are unverified.**

The element describes the participating coding agents, so a first-party ACP adapter belongs in its known-harness inventory if the cited catalog and adapter contain what the reviewer reports. “Any registered or user-supplied ACP command” does not adequately document a separately supplied adapter. However, neither `crates/roundtable-web/src/tables.rs` nor `adapters/openrouter-acp/src/adapter.ts` is supplied. OpenRouter's absence from `builtin()` (lines 78–90) establishes nothing about a separate web catalog.

**Change:** Add an explicit investigation entry: “Reported first-party harness: `openrouter-acp`; verify catalog placement in `crates/roundtable-web/src/tables.rs:76–99` and protocol declaration in `adapters/openrouter-acp/src/adapter.ts:3`.” After inspecting those files, replace “reported” with the verified behavior and record its launch path and protocol version. Do not add OpenRouter to this launcher's built-in list solely to make the lists match: the finding cites a different catalog, which may already supply it.

## GF2 — Pinned fallback versions omitted

**Decision: Accept. Confirmed directly.**

`builtin()` constructs these exact commands (lines 79–88):

| Harness | Built-in command |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.101.0` |
| Codex | `npx -y @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@2.5.0` |
| Pi | `npx -y pi-acp@0.0.34` |
| OpenCode | `npx -y opencode-ai@1.19.5 acp` |

**Change:** Record this table in `investigations`, tied to the supplied snapshot. Describe selection precisely: a registry fetch, HTTP-status, or JSON-decoding error returns the built-in catalog with a warning (lines 215–230). A successfully decoded registry is parsed first, then built-ins whose IDs are absent are appended (lines 221–228). A present ID suppresses its fallback even if that registry entry is unavailable; this is not fallback after a failed agent launch. The pins apply to built-in commands, not every launch. Registry entries can use registry packages or an installed binary whose version differs (lines 117–130).

No launcher change is needed. In particular, package versions are not evidence of ACP wire-protocol versions, and a built-in `npx` command does not guarantee operation without network access.

## GF3 — v1 URI versus claimed v2 operation

**Decision: Accept as a documentation ambiguity, not a demonstrated protocol mismatch.**

A v1 overview may be a useful reference even if other versions are supported. The URI alone neither limits the harness to v1 nor disproves the author's account of v2 runs. This file contains no protocol negotiation. Its registry URL's `/v1/` identifies the registry endpoint and does not establish the agents' ACP wire versions.

**Change:** Label the existing URI explicitly as the ACP v1 reference. If the v2 claims are retained, add the exact versioned v2 specification or draft they mean and cite negotiation evidence from the runs. Until that evidence is supplied, qualify v2 as an author-reported observation rather than describing dual-version support as verified. Do not replace the URI with an assumed v2 URL or change launcher code.

## GF4 — Evidence only covers launching

**Decision: Accept. Confirmed evidence limitation.**

The only supplied module selects launch specifications; it does not initialize agents, create sessions, set session configuration, send prompts, or consume updates. Its tests (lines 274–339) cover launch resolution, environment filtering, and command parsing. They do not substantiate the RPC list, run history, or the registry-wide version claim.

**Change:** Preserve the want as a requirement of `code.client.agent`, clearly separated from verified implementation behavior. Attach RPC-client implementation references and representative initialize/session/update traces when available. For the historical claims, cite run artifacts with dates, harness releases, and negotiated protocol versions; for the registry audit, cite its scope and evidence. Mark these claims unverified in this snapshot until then. Missing evidence is not proof the behavior is absent, so deleting the requirement or inventing missing code is unwarranted.

## GF5 — Consequence of the v2 “gap” unspecified

**Decision: Accept the missing compatibility explanation; do not accept the implied v2 requirement as established.**

“Only Claude Code and Codex use ACP v2” is a reported observation, not by itself a functional gap. A gap requires identifying a needed behavior that the other harnesses cannot provide. Neither the launcher's selection logic nor its package pins establish which protocol versions Roundtable requires or supports. The author's reported OpenCode v1 run also does not prove that every required operation works on v1.

**Change:** Replace the unexplained gap with a compatibility status that separates requirements, observations, and unknowns. State which negotiated versions the host supports and which required operations work for each tested harness/release, supported by client code and traces. Identify any concrete v1 limitation and its handling, such as capability checks, omission of an optional operation, or a clear unsupported-operation error. If no required behavior is missing, move the source-audit observation out of `gaps`. Pending evidence, use: “The author reports mixed ACP versions in recorded runs; the host's supported versions and any v1 limitations are not established by the supplied launcher.” No protocol upgrade is justified by this finding alone.

## GF6 — RPC method list lacks version and capability scope

**Decision: Accept the contract-clarity concern; version-dependent differences are not demonstrated here.**

The method list states the desired session workflow but does not distinguish mandatory operations from optional configuration or identify the protocol contract under which they are available. A list of method names alone cannot prove that v1 and v2 differ for those methods. `set_config_option` should also be checked against the actual wire method name and client API before the description treats it as an RPC name.

**Change:** Document the exact RPC names, supported protocol revision(s), and required capabilities alongside the want. State whether configuration is required or conditional and what the client does when an agent lacks it. Verify the session working directory and update/completion behavior in the client implementation. If that inspection finds unconditional calls to unsupported operations, fix the client to negotiate/check support or report incompatibility clearly. This is a conditional code recommendation, not a proven bug in `launch.rs`.

## GF7 — Pi has no run explanation or support status

**Decision: Accept the missing status; the reason cannot be inferred.**

Pi is explicitly offered by `builtin()` at `pi-acp@0.0.34` (line 87). That proves a launch recipe exists. Availability checks for built-ins establish the runner's presence (lines 195–198), not authentication, successful sessions, or feature compatibility. The author's “Pi has never run” needs a bounded scope; the launcher cannot verify a historical negative.

**Change:** Say: “Pi has a built-in launch recipe. The author reports no Pi runs in the recorded-run set as of 2026-11-07; runtime compatibility is unverified. The reason for no recorded run is not documented.” Add the actual reason if records establish it. Do not label Pi unsupported, broken, or fully supported solely from its catalog entry or lack of reported runs. No code change follows.

## GF8 — “Checked by their source” is ambiguous

**Decision: Accept.**

It is unclear which registry entries, repository revisions, and protocol declarations were inspected, or whether “version” means a package release, SDK dependency, declared protocol constant, or negotiated wire version. Those are different forms of evidence.

**Change:** Replace the phrase with a dated audit reference listing the registry snapshot and included agents, each harness release or commit, inspected file/symbol, and the conclusion that evidence supports. Keep source-declared protocol versions separate from versions observed during initialization. If no such audit record is available, use: “The author reports a source inspection dated 2026-11-07; the inspected registry scope, harness revisions, and protocol evidence are not supplied.” Remove or qualify the exclusive “only” claim until the audit supports its stated scope.

## Cross-cutting contradictions

Four fixes above, taken at face value, would write a falsehood into `element.md`. These are
the specific sentences to avoid; they matter because the other findings' advice ("record
exactly what the code proves") is only safe if these are respected.

1. **"tables.rs / adapter.ts prove OpenRouter is ACP v1."** Neither file is in the snapshot,
   and the adapter's own protocol declaration is exactly what is cited, not shown. Record it
   as *reported*, with the file/line, or omit the version. (GF1)
2. **"the built-ins fall back only when the registry is unreachable."** False. `autoselect`
   (222–231) also appends built-ins when the registry succeeds but omits their id, and a
   present id suppresses the fallback even if that registry entry is unavailable. Record both
   conditions. (GF2)
3. **"the URI is wrong / swap it for v2."** Swapping it misrepresents the v1 harnesses the
   element covers. Label the v1 URI and add the v2 document under `references` instead. (GF3)
4. **"acp-host launches v1 harnesses just like v2."** True in the launcher (no version gate),
   but do not upgrade that into "v1 harnesses are supported": the launcher neither reads a
   negotiated version nor any RPC, so launchability is not compatibility. State the
   negotiation question as open unless client evidence is supplied. (GF5)

## Disposition

These findings call for description and evidence improvements. GF2 and GF4 are directly confirmed by the supplied code; GF1's specific catalog and protocol assertions require the missing files. GF3 and GF5–GF8 correctly identify ambiguities without establishing protocol defects. Keep the existing launcher unchanged on this evidence. Resolve the missing-evidence items through explicit qualification now and replace those qualifications with cited results when the relevant artifacts are available.
