roundtable.resolution:
# Resolution of the review findings — element `upstream.system.reputation` ("accolades")

Decisions by **ExactLizard**. Each finding gets a verdict, the reason, and the concrete change
to the description (`element.md`) or to the code. "Right" means the finding identifies a real,
inspectable defect in the description or a real discrepancy with the code; it does not mean I
endorse every clause of the finding verbatim — where a clause is wrong I say so.

## Scope and method (read this first)

The `source/` folder copied for this review contains exactly three files:

- `crates/roundtable-web/src/app.rs`
- `crates/roundtable/src/turn.rs`
- `docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md`

The findings cite `mcp.rs`, `engine.rs`, `index.html`, `stages.py`, `store.py`, `runner.py`,
`prompts.xml`, `roundtable-accolades.md` and `project_agent.txt`. **None of these are in the
copy.** Claims that depend on them are marked *unverifiable here*; where the receiving side is
visible in `app.rs`/`turn.rs` I verify that instead. `roundtable-agent-ratings.md` itself has
dangling `../../src/metaform/...` links (lines 5, 144) and a dangling link to
`roundtable-accolades.md` (line 160), so even the in-repo doc does not resolve to the primary
source — consistent with the `elephant.gaps` note.

Verified in-repo facts used below:

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `accolades.jsonl` is opened under `ROUNDTABLE_HOME` (else `HOME/.roundtable`) | `app.rs:60-69` |
| `roundtable.rating` events go to `save_rating` (points) only | `app.rs:98-102`, `500-509` |
| `roundtable.feedback` events go to `save_feedback` **and** are appended verbatim to `accolades.jsonl` | `app.rs:103-111`, `535-545` |
| Feedback adds no points; end-of-table ratings do | `app.rs:533-534`, `703-704` (test), `500-509` |
| Identity profiles are local files keyed by genesis session, with `points`, `ratings`, `feedback`, `contexts` | `app.rs:426-495`, `457-459` |
| `points` feed `FileIdentities::profile` → `Profile.score` | `app.rs:483-495` |
| Returning agents are shown `session_profile` (score, ratings, sessions) | `turn.rs:37-50` |
| End-of-table rating round computes points per target via `rules::rating_points` | `turn.rs:447-485`, `471` |
| `finish_ratings` builds the session ranking and a cross-session `rating` from the stored profile | `turn.rs:516-544` |
| Points sort the identities list | `app.rs:547-568`, `567` |
| The 0–5 stars + boolean bonus scale and the 10/20/30/40 (+5) weighting are documented | `roundtable-agent-ratings.md:60-61, 98-113, 115-122` |

One framing point that governs GF1, GF6 and GF8: this is an **`upstream.*`** element. Its own
`investigations` note says accolades/identity/return-weighting "reach beyond one Roundtable" and
are "treated as a platform service Roundtable feeds". So the Rust code is legitimately the
*feed* (the `code.server.tool` want) plus a local identity store, not necessarily the whole
upstream service. `elephant.built: "Not built here"` is therefore not simply false — it is
**unqualified and misleading**, which is its own defect. The fix is in the description.

---

## GF1 — Blocker, `elephant.built` "Not built here" contradicts the code

**Verdict: RIGHT, with a qualification on the framing. Change the description, not the code.**

Why right: the want is concretely realized in the copied code. `code.server.tool`'s "let
participants reward one another's good conduct" is realized as the `roundtable.feedback` path:
`app.rs:103-111` consumes the event, `save_feedback` (`app.rs:535-545`) writes it to the
recipient identity's `feedback` list, and the same raw line is appended to
`ROUNDTABLE_HOME/accolades.jsonl` (`app.rs:69`). The identity is local and persistent
(`app.rs:426-495`). Session ranking, a cross-session `rating`, and the profile score shown to a
returning agent are built (`turn.rs:37-50, 516-544`). A reader who takes "Not built here" at
face value would conclude there is no in-repo realisation of the want at all, which is wrong;
that is a legitimate Blocker-level contradiction.

Qualification, and why it matters: GF1 says the want "is built as the MCP 'feedback' tool
(mcp.rs:22-36, 84-104) ... FeedbackGiven keyed by to_session (engine.rs:882-898)". Those files
are **not in the copy**, so the sending side is *unverifiable here*; what I can confirm is the
receiving side (`roundtable.feedback`, `to_session`/`to_name` in `save_feedback`, and the
`/mcp/{table}/{seat}` participant-tools endpoint at `app.rs:158, 370-392` dispatching to
`roundtable::mcp::handle`). Also, "Not built here" is defensible if read narrowly as "the
upstream/platform accolades service and its return weighting are not in this repo" — the
`investigations` note already says as much. So the contradiction is with the **unqualified**
wording, not with a defensible narrower reading.

What should change — in `element.md`:
1. Rewrite `elephant.built` to split covered from missing (see the consolidated patch at the
   end). State that Roundtable does build the tool, `accolades.jsonl`, local identity profiles,
   the end-of-table rating→points, the session ranking, the cross-session rating and the profile
   score shown to the agent.
2. Move "only the return weighting is missing" into `elephant.gaps` as an explicit, named gap,
   and soften the owner statement's "It weights them higher than other agents to return into the
   project" to *, which is intended but not implemented here* — otherwise the description still
   asserts a behaviour the code does not have. GF1 itself concedes this is the one missing piece.
3. Do **not** implement return weighting as part of this review. The element is an upstream
   service and the `investigations` note says "where it lives and how the weighting is applied is
   not yet specified"; inventing a weighting rule in this repo would pre-empt an unspecified
   platform decision. Record the gap instead.

## GF2 — Major, `Properties.uri` / `archaeology.path` point at a non-existent in-repo path

**Verdict: RIGHT. Change the description.**

Why: `Properties.uri` = `archaeology/src/metaform/modules/roundtables/roundtable/resources/prompts.xml`
and the `archaeology.finding.path` cite the same file. Neither `archaeology/` nor `prompts.xml`
exists in the copy. The only in-repo owner-source artefact is
`docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md`, which reproduces the scorecard prompt (lines
53-96) and the weighted-points formula (98-113). GF2 is also right that `roundtable-accolades.md`
— cited at line 160 of that doc — is absent. Additional evidence GF2 did not give: the in-repo
doc's own `../../src/metaform/...` links (lines 5, 144) are dangling too, and line 160 says the
primary sources/tests live in "the full archive" — i.e. outside this repo. So no in-repo path
resolves to the primary source.

What should change — in `element.md`: either
- (a) repoint `Properties.uri` and `archaeology.path` to
  `docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md` **with a note** that this is a paraphrase
  of the owner's archive, not the primary source (which is external), or
- (b) keep the archaeology path but mark it explicitly as an **external** reference
  (`~/roundtable/archaeology/...`) and add a one-line convention for external archaeology
  paths.

Do (a) and note the archive is external; doing only (a) without the note would just trade one
misleading path for another. Coordinate with GF7 — these two must be resolved together, not with
two contradictory edits.

## GF3 — Major, two undocumented data paths into/out of "accolades"

**Verdict: RIGHT. Change the description (documentation gap); no code change needed.**

Why: verified exactly as stated. `accolades.jsonl` receives **only** `roundtable.feedback`
events (`app.rs:103-111`) — the mid-table `feedback` tool — and those explicitly add no points
(`app.rs:533-534`; test `app.rs:703-704`). End-of-table `roundtable.rating` events add points via
`save_rating` (`app.rs:98-102, 500-509`) and are **not** appended to `accolades.jsonl`. The
element is named "accolades", yet it never mentions `accolades.jsonl`, never says the thing that
literally carries the name is the *pointless* mid-table feedback stream, and never says standing
comes from a *different* stream. That is a real, non-obvious discrepancy a reader cannot resolve
from the description. Severity Major is fair given the element's whole subject is this concept.

What should change — in `element.md`: add a short "Data flows" note (see patch): state that an
accolade record is the raw `roundtable.feedback` line appended to `accolades.jsonl` and stored
in the identity's `feedback` list (raw ratings + note, no points), whereas points/cumulative
score come from the separate end-of-table rating and live in the identity's `points`/`ratings`.
This also supplies most of the definition GF5 asks for.

## GF4 — Nit, nothing weights agents for return; make "not yet specified" concrete

**Verdict: PARTLY RIGHT. The substantive point is right; one clause is wrong. Change the description; correct the clause.**

Why the substantive point is right: no code in the copy selects, weights, or prioritises an agent
for return into a project. `investigations` says "how the weighting is applied is not yet
specified" — true, but vague. Recording the concrete negative is worthwhile and consistent with
GF1's "only the return weighting is missing".

Why one clause is wrong: "Points are used **only** to sort the identities list (app.rs:547-568)
and to label the resume picker (index.html:416-417)". That is an overstatement I can disprove
from the copy: `points` is read by `FileIdentities::profile` into `Profile.score`
(`app.rs:483-495`), which drives `session_profile` shown to a returning agent (`turn.rs:37-50`)
and the cross-session `rating` in `finish_ratings` (`turn.rs:521-533`). GF1 itself cites those as
built. `index.html` is not in the copy, so the resume-picker label is *unverifiable here*. Points
have at least three consumers, not one.

What should change — in `element.md`: in `investigations` (or `elephant.gaps`), replace "not yet
specified" with a concrete statement: no return-weighting exists; points currently feed (i) the
profile score / cross-session rating shown to the agent (`turn.rs:37-50, 516-544`), (ii) the
sort of `/api/identities` (`app.rs:567`), and (iii) — if the resume picker is confirmed — its
label; none of these constitutes weighting an agent for return. Do not repeat GF4's "only".

## GF5 — Major, "accolade" is never defined

**Verdict: RIGHT. Change the description.**

Why: the word appears in `owner_statements` and the want, but the element gives no definition and
never says how a rating becomes an accolade. A reader can only paraphrase the owner. This is the
root comprehension defect and it amplifies GF3, GF6 and GF8.

What should change — in `element.md`: add a definition, and I can supply it from the code rather
than leaving it abstract:

> An **accolade** is one peer-feedback record: a participant's `feedback` rating of another's
> conduct (0–5 in Efficient, Alert & Aware, Thorough, Coordination, plus a boolean bonus and a
> free-text note), emitted as a `roundtable.feedback` event during the table. It is appended
> verbatim to `ROUNDTABLE_HOME/accolades.jsonl` and stored in the recipient identity's
> `feedback` list. An accolade carries no points; cumulative standing ("reputation") comes from
> the separate end-of-table rating. Recognition is therefore the recorded feedback stream, not
> the score.

That definition also settles "how ratings become one": the mid-table feedback tool is the
accolade path; the end-of-table scorecard is the scoring path. If the map author intends
"accolade" to mean the *upstream recognition/award* instead (per `elephant.design`, "agents earned
recognition"), the description must say that explicitly and mark the in-repo `accolades.jsonl` as
the feed, not the award — either reading is acceptable, but one must be chosen.

## GF6 — Major, `code.server.tool` is never introduced; the want's function is vague

**Verdict: RIGHT. Change the description.**

Why: `code.server.tool` appears only in the single "wants" bullet, with no introduction anywhere
in the element, and "Records a participant's rating of another participant's behavior toward
accolades and identity" does not say what the dependency delivers today. Combined with
`elephant.built: "Not built here"`, the wants section describes a dependency on an element the
description says is absent — an internal inconsistency (GF1 establishes the tool is present).

What should change — in `element.md`: introduce `code.server.tool` with its concrete in-repo
identity (the participant `feedback` MCP tool served at `/mcp/{table}/{seat}`, `app.rs:158,
370-392`) and rewrite the want's Function to state today's deliverable: one `roundtable.feedback`
event per rating → recipient identity's `feedback` list + a line in `accolades.jsonl`. Replace
"toward accolades and identity" with that. This is a description fix; GF1's fix removes the
"not built here" contradiction that makes GF6 read as a paradox.

## GF7 — Major, relative-path header vs. external archaeology gap; "archaeology" undefined

**Verdict: RIGHT. Change the description.**

Why: genuine internal contradiction. The header says "Paths are relative to the Roundtable
folder", so `archaeology/src/...` reads as an in-repo path; `elephant.gaps` says it is in
`~/roundtable/archaeology`, "which is not in this repo". Both cannot hold. "Archaeology" is used
as a layer name and a directory name with no definition, and the source cannot be found in the
copy (GF2). A reader cannot locate the primary material.

What should change — in `element.md`: pick one convention and apply it to header, `Properties.uri`,
`archaeology.path` and `elephant.gaps` together. Preferred: define "archaeology" once as "recovered
material from the owner's earlier Roundtable versions, held in the owner's archive outside this
repository" and prefix external references explicitly (e.g. `~/roundtable/archaeology/...`),
while stating that the header's "relative to the Roundtable folder" rule applies **only** to
in-repo paths. Then repoint the citable in-repo artefact to
`docs/owner-sources/roundtable-agent-ratings.md`. GF2 and GF7 are one edit, not two.

## GF8 — Major, "peer ratings cover part of it" is vague; scale never reconciled

**Verdict: PARTLY RIGHT. Right that the description is vague; wrong about which parts are missing. Change the description; correct the parenthetical.**

Why right: `elephant.built` says "Peer ratings (code.rating.peer) cover part of it" without
enumerating covered vs. missing, and the element never reconciles the archaeology 0–5-star /
boolean-bonus scale with the current one. Both are real comprehension gaps.

Why the parenthetical is wrong: GF8 lists "cross-session rating, profile score, weighting for
return" as the ambiguous covered/missing set. But GF1 (and the code) show **cross-session rating
and profile score are built** — `turn.rs:37-50` (`session_profile`) and `turn.rs:516-544`
(`finish_ratings` uses the stored profile's `score`). Only **weighting for return** is missing.
Repeating GF8's list verbatim would reintroduce the very error GF1 corrects.

On the scale, the description can be reconciled concretely from the in-repo doc: the scale is
unchanged — 0–5 stars in the four categories plus a boolean `bonus`, weighted 10/20/30/40 with
+5 for the bonus (max 105 for one rating) — documented at
`roundtable-agent-ratings.md:60-61, 98-113, 115-122`, and still the shape of the `feedback`/rating
tools. The doc also records two real differences worth citing: the roundtable prompt delivers the
scale *without* the detailed worker rubric or bonus explanation (lines 113, 156-158), and a
stale tasks README still claims an initial 100 / cap 105 (lines 156-158). So the scale is not
"never reconciled" in the repo — it is reconciled in the owner-source doc; the *element* simply
doesn't reference it.

What should change — in `element.md`: rewrite `elephant.built` as an explicit covered/missing
list (see patch) and add one line pointing to `roundtable-agent-ratings.md` for the scale,
rubric-delivery difference and README drift.

## GF9 — Major, undefined jargon in `investigations`

**Verdict: RIGHT in substance, but fix by cross-reference, not by expanding this element. Change the description.**

Why: `topogee`, `deterministic agent identity`, `post-retirement recall`, `platform service`,
`return into a project` and agent `retirement` appear in the `investigations` note with no
definition in this element, and none of them appear in the copied code. A reader cannot tell what
comparison is being drawn. That is a real comprehension defect.

Critical nuance / scope: these are cross-references to **other elements of the functional map**

## GF10 — Nit, no "role"; `upstream.` prefix and metadata fields unexplained

investigations.note: The owner's WSL2 kernel 6.18 has CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL, CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF (/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux present), CONFIG_BPF_EVENTS and CONFIG_UPROBE_EVENTS, so eBPF tracing is possible. /sys/kernel/tracing is not readable as the normal user, so capture needs root or CAP_BPF/CAP_PERFMON on the capture binary. agentsight-capture is on crates.io (last updated 2026-10-23), MIT licensed; repo eunomia-bpf/agentsight last pushed 2026-10-31.

decisions.decision: Monitoring fails open: without the privileges for eBPF capture, the monitor runs with what it can observe unprivileged (process exit, ACP traffic) and publishes that capture is unavailable. Granting capabilities is a one-time setup step the owner chooses, never something Roundtable does itself.

elephant.design: AgentSight observes agent processes with eBPF.
elephant.built: Used through agentsight-capture by the activity monitor.
gaps: Needs root.

findings.finding: 'Without the privileges ... the monitor runs with what it can observe unprivileged (process exit, ACP traffic) and publishes that capture is unavailable' is false. Without effective root, attach returns Err before anything starts, so no Monitor exists and nothing is observed (crates/agent-monitor/src/capture.rs:40-42; lib.rs:49-53). Process exit is reported by acp-host's HarnessExited, not by the monitor (crates/roundtable/src/engine.rs:465-466).

'Granting capabilities is a one-time setup step' and 'capture needs root or CAP_BPF/CAP_PERFMON on the capture binary' contradict the code. It requires effective uid 0 and rejects a process holding CAP_BPF and CAP_PERFMON without root (crates/agent-monitor/src/capture.rs:179-209; test at capture.rs:506-509). There is also no lasting capture binary to grant capabilities to: the probes are unpacked by BinaryExtractor while the monitor runs (capture.rs:50-52).

'Observable model-provider activity': sslsniff is limited to the harness pid, not its children, and AgentSight's LLM classifier is not used (crates/agent-monitor/src/lib.rs:33-45; capture.rs:103-114).

Unstated dependency details: (1) The version is pinned exactly at agentsight-capture =1.0.35 (crates/agent-monitor/Cargo.toml:18); the investigation only mentions the crates.io update date. (2) The dependency is optional behind the default `agentsight` feature (Cargo.toml:8-12). (3) The probes ship prebuilt, so building needs no clang or headers, but at run time they need libelf, libz and libzstd (lib.rs:55-58).

The probe settings are not recorded: process probe `-p <pid> -m 2 --trace-fs --trace-net` seeded with the pid family (capture.rs:55-58); sslsniff with `--binary-path` when the executable embeds its own TLS library (capture.rs:105-114); HTTPParser with raw data disabled (capture.rs:119-123).
The decision says monitoring fails open with unprivileged observation; the gap says 'Needs root' and the code's attach fails without root. The current behaviour is unclear.

The investigation says root or CAP_BPF/CAP_PERFMON is enough; the elephant layer says root, and the code shows capabilities without root still fall back to sudo -n. The documented setup would not work.
The 'one-time setup step the owner chooses' has no steps or link, and it conflicts with the root service under HoldOn named in code.monitor.activity.
'Observable model-provider activity' is vague: the document doesn't say how provider traffic is seen (e.g. TLS capture) or when it can't be.
Only the owner's WSL2 machine was checked; the platform limits in general are not stated or linked.

paraphrase.egm-codebase-details: AgentSight, used through the agentsight-capture crate pinned at version 1.0.35, is the eBPF tracer behind Roundtable's activity monitor. Roundtable runs its `process` probe, which follows the harness and its children for process, file and network activity, and its `sslsniff` probe, whose TLS records go through AgentSight's HTTP parser. It also uses AgentSight's timestamp normalizer and its prebuilt probe programs.
paraphrase.egm-comprehension: AgentSight is an outside eBPF tracing tool, used through the agentsight-capture crate, that captures process, subprocess, file, network and model-provider activity of harness processes. The owner's kernel supports it, but tracing needs privileges. The recorded decision says monitoring fails open and granting privileges is the owner's choice.

roundtable.resolution:
# AgentSight review resolutions

Prepared by SereneSpear from `element.md` and the supplied source snapshot.

The appropriate immediate fix is to correct the description to match the current integration. The snapshot supports effective-root-only capture, explicit unavailability reporting, process-family tracing, and harness-PID TLS/HTTP metadata capture. It does not support an unprivileged capture mode or capability-only setup. Those would require separate implementation work if retained as requirements.

Evidence scope: only `source/crates/agent-monitor/src/capture.rs` and `source/crates/agent-monitor/Cargo.toml` are supplied. References below use their original repository paths. The reviewers also cite `lib.rs`, `engine.rs`, upstream implementation details, and a HoldOn service description that are absent here. Conclusions depending on those sources are explicitly qualified. No code changes or executable tests are required to write these decisions, and this snapshot has no workspace manifest with which to run the crate tests.

## GF1 — Accept the core finding; correct its overstatement

**Decision:** The decision layer incorrectly attributes unprivileged process-exit and ACP observation to this monitor. However, “nothing is observed” must not be read as “nothing is published.”

**Evidence:** `capture.rs:37–42` calls `fail(None, reason)` and returns `Err` before collecting processes or starting probes. `fail` calls `unavailable`. The included test `attach_without_root_publishes_the_reason` (`capture.rs:540–556`) explicitly expects the returned error to be published as `MonitorUnavailable`. The implementation of `unavailable` itself is in the missing `lib.rs`. The supplied capture implementation has no ACP fallback; its process-exit mapping (`capture.rs:236–240`) consumes probe records and therefore is unavailable when attachment is rejected.

**Change:** Replace “the monitor runs with what it can observe unprivileged” with: “When capture cannot attach, attachment returns `MonitorUnavailable` and publishes the reason; no capture session is started. Roundtable's ACP and harness-lifecycle reporting are separate mechanisms.” Confirm application continuation and the specific `HarnessExited` ownership against the full caller code before documenting them as verified behavior. Fail-open at the application boundary can coexist with failed monitor attachment; this snapshot proves the latter, not the former.

## GF2 — Accept

**Decision:** Capability-only setup is not supported by the current wrapper, regardless of what the kernel could permit.

**Evidence:** `privilege_shortfall` accepts effective UID 0 and rejects every other UID (`capture.rs:179–209`). Capability bits are read only to explain rejection. The test at `capture.rs:506–509` covers rejection with both CAP_BPF and CAP_PERFMON. The comment and diagnostic explain that upstream would otherwise use `sudo -n`; the wrapper rejects before reaching it. `BinaryExtractor::new()` obtains probe executables during attachment (`capture.rs:50–58`), and `Running` holds the extractor for the capture lifetime (`capture.rs:23–26`). There is no stable, administrator-installed probe path configured in this wrapper.

**Change:** Remove the capability-grant setup claim from the decision and qualify the investigation: kernel-level capability possibilities are not a supported deployment mode for this integration. Document that the current capture host must run with effective UID 0 and that the wrapper performs no escalation. Root is a prerequisite, not a guarantee that probes attach. Do not suggest applying file capabilities to the main application or transient probes as a working fix. Supporting capabilities requires changing both the local gate and upstream launch behavior, and supplying a deliberate probe installation/execution arrangement.

## GF3 — Accept the coverage limit; do not require an LLM classifier merely to observe HTTP

**Decision:** Process-family coverage must not imply equal TLS coverage. The absence of provider classification limits the meaning of “model-provider activity,” but does not prevent ordinary HTTP metadata from exposing a recognizable provider host.

**Evidence:** The process runner receives process-family seeds (`capture.rs:43–58`); the TLS runner receives only `-p <harness pid>` and no family seeds or child attachment logic (`capture.rs:103–114`). The analyzer pipeline constructs timestamp normalization and `HTTPParser`, with no LLM classifier (`capture.rs:117–132`). Published parsed observations contain request method, host, path and exchange ID, response status and exchange ID, and unfinished-exchange metadata (`capture.rs:265–286`). No parsed model, tokens, prompt or provider-specific classification is published.

**Change:** Narrow the want to “process-family activity and, where the TLS probe can instrument the harness PID, HTTP request/response metadata that may reveal provider contact.” Explicitly state that child-process provider requests are outside the configured TLS coverage and that no LLM semantic classification is performed. If descendant provider visibility is mandatory, add lifecycle-managed TLS attachment for relevant descendants and verify it with a harness whose child performs the request. Add classification only if semantic provider/model information is actually required.

## GF4 — Accept the dependency-documentation gap, with an evidence limit

**Decision:** The exact dependency and feature details are established; the prebuilt-probe and runtime-library claims need verification from the omitted source or pinned upstream package.

**Evidence:** `Cargo.toml:8–12` makes `agentsight` a default-enabled feature. Line 18 pins the optional dependency exactly to `agentsight-capture = "=1.0.35"`. The manifest comment says disabling the feature makes `Monitor::attach` report `MonitorUnavailable`; the feature-disabled implementation is not supplied. Runtime extraction is visible in `capture.rs:50–58`, but extraction alone does not prove which build tools or shared libraries are required. The cited `lib.rs:55–58` is absent.

**Change:** Record version `1.0.35`, exact pinning, default-enabled optional feature, and the documented no-feature unavailable behavior. Add verified build/runtime prerequisites for that pinned package. Specifically check the claim that probes ship prebuilt (so no probe compilation with clang/kernel headers is needed locally) and require libelf, libz and libzstd at runtime before presenting that list as authoritative. Do not silently substitute an upstream latest-version requirement for the pinned package's requirements. This finding does not justify changing the dependency or feature defaults.

## GF5 — Accept

**Decision:** Record the integration settings because they explain its observation scope and data handling.

**Evidence/change:** Add a compact configuration note covering:

- Process runner: `-p <harness pid> -m 2 --trace-fs --trace-net`, seeded from the harness and existing descendants; the source comment says the probe follows later descendants (`capture.rs:43–58`).
- TLS runner: `-p <harness pid>`; add `--binary-path <harness executable>` only when reading `/proc/<pid>/exe` succeeds and `binary_embeds_ssl` identifies embedded SSL (`capture.rs:103–114`). This is conditional, not a guarantee that all TLS implementations work.
- Normalize timestamps and pass TLS records through `HTTPParser::disable_raw_data()` (`capture.rs:117–132`). Bodies may be parsed internally, but parsed observations publish only the selected metadata (`capture.rs:118`, `265–286`). Do not describe this as “no plaintext is ever captured or processed.”

No code change is needed for this documentation finding.

## GF6 — Accept; resolve together with GF1 and GF2

**Decision:** The decision and gap currently describe different layers without saying so, creating a real contradiction.

**Change:** State consistently: capture requires effective root; rejection reports capture unavailable and produces no running capture session. Application-level continuation, ACP messages and harness exit reporting must be documented under their actual owners after checking their caller code. Replace the bare “Needs root” gap with “Current wrapper requires effective UID 0; capability-only and unprivileged capture modes are unsupported.” Do not implement a dummy monitor solely to make the old wording appear true.

## GF7 — Accept the setup contradiction; reject the claimed executed fallback

**Decision:** The investigation's capability alternative does not work through this integration. But the wrapper does **not** actually fall back to `sudo -n`.

**Evidence:** `capture.rs:40–42` rejects before probe startup; `capture.rs:179–209` explains why upstream's non-root launch policy causes this restriction. A diagnostic about an upstream code path is not evidence that the wrapper executes that path.

**Change:** Align investigation, decision and elephant gap around effective-root-only capture, with no automatic escalation, as in GF2. Keep the historical WSL2 kernel observations as dated machine-specific evidence, not as proof that capability setup works. This prevents users from following an ineffective capability recipe or expecting a sudo prompt.

## GF8 — Accept missing operational guidance; the claimed HoldOn conflict is unproven

**Decision:** “One-time setup” is not actionable and currently points at an unsupported capability mechanism. However, a deliberately provisioned root service and owner-controlled setup are not inherently contradictory. No HoldOn service configuration or description is supplied to establish an actual conflict.

**Change:** Replace the capability setup promise with a link to the actual deployment instructions for whichever component hosts capture. If HoldOn hosts it, document the real service name/configuration, effective user, harness/PID visibility and startup procedure; otherwise document the real hosting arrangement. State that the owner provisions privileges and the wrapper does not escalate. Verify that the deployment actually calls attachment from the privileged context. Do not invent a service name, command or service implementation from the review text, or recommend running unrelated components as root to fill this documentation gap.

## GF9 — Accept; resolve with GF3 and GF5

**Decision:** “Observable model-provider activity” needs a mechanism and explicit boundaries.

**Change:** Explain that an sslsniff probe instruments supported TLS library calls for the harness PID, followed by HTTP parsing and publication of selected metadata. Embedded SSL may cause the executable to be passed as `--binary-path`. Provider contact may be inferred from host/path; the integration does not classify provider/model semantics. Missing privileges, failed probes, unsupported TLS instrumentation, traffic originating in children or other processes, and traffic the HTTP parser cannot parse can prevent this view. Network summaries remain a separate observation and do not guarantee provider identification. Use these bounds instead of implying general visibility into model calls.

## GF10 — Accept

**Decision:** The dated WSL2 check is useful evidence for one machine, not a supported-platform specification.

**Evidence:** `missing_privileges` explicitly rejects non-Linux at runtime and reads Linux `/proc/self/status` (`capture.rs:168–176`); attachment reads the process table, and TLS executable resolution uses `/proc` (`capture.rs:43`, `108`). The supplied files do not establish architecture support, minimum kernel version, a non-Linux build guarantee or an exhaustive eBPF feature matrix.

**Change:** Document Linux runtime capture, usable `/proc` and target-process visibility, effective-root requirements, and compatible kernel/probe support. Preserve the investigation's kernel configuration/BTF observations as dated local checks. Link verified requirements for the pinned upstream version, including supported probe architectures and kernel prerequisites, rather than extrapolating them from kernel 6.18 on one WSL2 host. State that root alone does not overcome missing kernel features or host restrictions. No portable fallback capture is implemented here.

## Consistent replacement account

Use this core wording across the decision, want and elephant layers, supplemented by the dependency and deployment details above:

> AgentSight capture uses the default-enabled `agentsight` feature and the exact `agentsight-capture` version 1.0.35. The current wrapper requires a Linux capture host running with effective UID 0 and a compatible kernel/runtime environment; it neither supports capability-only startup nor escalates privileges. If attachment fails, it reports capture unavailable instead of starting a capture session. When available, the process probe tracks the seeded harness process family and later descendants. The separate TLS probe targets the harness PID and feeds HTTP parsing; it publishes selected HTTP metadata, not LLM classification or request/response bodies. TLS failure can leave process capture running. ACP and harness-lifecycle reporting belong to separate parts of Roundtable.

The independent TLS failure behavior is explicit in `capture.rs:90–100`: it reports TLS unavailability and still returns the running process capture. This is a supported partial-capture mode and should not be confused with the nonexistent unprivileged fallback.
